The men of Jabesh-gilead had shown themselves kind to the former king of Israel, and for this they were commended by the new king. David did not harbor a grudge toward the memory of Saul even though he had suffered severely at Saul’s hand. By recognizing the kindness and valor of those who had given their allegiance to Saul, David won the allegiance of these men to himself.

6.zh:
你們既行了這事，願耶和華以慈愛誠實待你們，我也要為此厚待你們。

**厚待。**大衛保證作基列雅比人的朋友和保護者，正如在他以前的掃羅一樣。這座城邑容易受到來自東部沙漠地區的攻擊，所以百姓可能會有需要新王幫助的時候。大衛想讓他們知道，他不會因為他們忠於掃羅就對他們抱有敵意。他們可以仰賴他，就像仰賴掃羅一樣。
6.en: **Requite you.** David pledged that he would be the friend and protector of the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead even as Saul had been before him. Since the city was vulnerable to attack from the eastern desert, the time might come when the people would need the help of the new king. David wanted them to know that he held nothing against them because of their loyalty to Saul, and that they could count upon him even as they had counted on Saul.

7.zh:
現在你們的主─掃羅死了，猶大家已經膏我作他們的王，所以你們要剛強奮勇。

**你們要剛強奮勇。**大衛邀請基列雅比人對他剛強奮勇，就像他們對以色列以前的王剛強奮勇一樣。
7.en: **Be ye valiant.** An invitation from David for the men of Jabesh-gilead to show themselves as faithful and valiant to him as they had shown themselves faithful to Israel’s former king.

8.zh:
掃羅的元帥尼珥的兒子押尼珥，曾將掃羅的兒子伊施波設帶過河，到瑪哈念，

**掃羅的元帥。**掃羅為王時，立自己的叔叔押尼珥作他軍隊的統帥（撒上14:50）。押尼珥因此既藉著血緣又藉著官職與掃羅家緊密聯合。他曾與掃羅一起追趕大衛，現在不願意他曾追趕了那麼久的人繼承掃羅統治的國度。押尼珥從未忘記大衛曾指責他在守衛時睡著了（撒上26:7-16）。他驕傲，圖謀報復，野心勃勃，決心走自己的路，不讓大衛作為耶和華的受膏者施行統治。
**尼珥的兒子。**見撒上14:50註釋。
**伊施波設。**掃羅最小的兒子。掃羅的其他兒子已在基利波戰役中與他一同被殺了（撒上31:2）。他的名字（在撒上14:49中縮略為“亦施韋”）可能最初是伊施巴力（代上8:33；9:39），意思是“巴力的人”，因為沒有王會給自己的兒子起名為“伊施波設”，意思是“羞恥的人。”
**瑪哈念。**直譯是“兩營。”這座城鎮在約旦河東，但其地點還不確定。人們提出的兩個地點之一在基列雅比的東邊。雅各在離開拉班後過雅博河前遇見上帝的使者時，給那地起了這個名字（創32:1,2）。它是利未人的一座城（書21:38），位於國家的東部地域，比較安全，不易受到非利士人的攻擊，也不易被大衛攻取，要是大衛要鎮壓他對手的話。大衛後來逃避押沙龍時，以瑪哈唸作為他的避難所（撒下17:24）。示撒的勝利碑銘Mhnm稱這座城為Mhnm，用埃及的無元音象形文字寫成（見王上14:25註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–23節）**。《先祖與先知》第699頁。
8.en:
**The son of Ner.** See on 1 Sam. 14:50.
Captain of Saul’s host. When Saul became king he made his uncle Abner commander in chief of his army (1 Sam. 14:50). Abner was thus, by the ties of blood and of office, strongly attached to the house of Saul. He had been with Saul in the pursuit of David, and was not now willing that the man he had so long hunted should succeed to the kingdom over which Saul had reigned. Abner never forgot the rebuke David gave him for sleeping on guard (1 Sam. 26:7–16). He was proud, vengeful, and ambitious, determined to have his own way rather than to allow David to rule as the anointed of the Lord.
Ish-bosheth. The youngest of Saul’s four sons. The other sons were slain with Saul at the battle of Mt. Gilboa (1 Sam. 31:2). His name (shortened to Ishui in 1 Sam. 14:49) was probably originally Esh-baal (1 Chron. 8:33; 9:39), meaning “man of Baal,” for no king would name his son “Ish-bosheth,” meaning “man of shame.”
Mahanaim. Literally, “two camps.” This town was on the east side of the Jordan, but its site has not been identified. One of two suggested sites is east of Jabesh-gilead. Jacob gave the name to the place when the angels of God met him after he had parted from Laban and before he crossed the Jabbok (Gen. 32:1, 2). It was a Levitical city (Joshua 21:38). Located in the eastern section of the country, it was in comparative safety from the attacks of the Philistines and of the forces of David should David choose to suppress his rival. When David later fled from Absalom he made Mahanaim his place of refuge (2 Sam. 17:24). The city is mentioned in Shishak’s victory inscription as Mḥnm, in the Egyptian vowelless hieroglyphic script (see on 1 Kings 14:25).

9.zh:
立他作王，治理基列、亞書利、耶斯列、以法蓮、便雅憫，和以色列眾人。

**立他作王。**伊施波設加冕為以色列王是出於押尼珥的堅強意志。押尼珥因長久與掃羅聯合而恨惡上帝所揀選作王的人。他沒有原則，專顧自己低級自私的利益，而不是百姓的利益或耶和華的旨意。他寧可讓國家分裂，民族不幸，也不願接受大衛為王。
**治理基列。**伊施波設所統治的領土從首都周圍的地區延伸到更遠的地區。除了基列之外，所有其它的地點都在約旦河西。便雅憫在這個區域的南部，耶路撒冷以北。
**亞書利。**不清楚是指什麼人。可能是指亞設支派的人（見士1:32）。七十士譯本是“Thasiri”（他斯利），拉丁文武加大譯本和亞蘭文譯本是 “Geshur”（革書珥）。伊施波設先是在基列被接受，後來把統治擴展到“以色列眾人”。
9.en:
**Made him king.** The coronation of Ish-bosheth as king over Israel was due to the determined purpose of Abner. Long associated with Saul, Abner had come to hate the man whom God had chosen as king. He was unprincipled, a man who was devoted to his own low, selfish interests rather than the interests of the people or the will of the Lord. He would rather bring about a division of the kingdom and distress upon the nation than accept David as king.
Over Gilead. The description of the territory over which Ish-bosheth ruled begins with the region surrounding the capital, Mahanaim, and then extends to the more distant areas. With the exception of Gilead all the sites are on the west of the Jordan, with Benjamin in the south in the area north of Jerusalem.
Ashurites. It is not clear what people are meant. The reference may be to members of the tribe of Asher (see Judges 1:32). The LXX has “Thasiri” and the Vulgate and the Syriac “Geshur.” Ish-bosheth was accepted first in Gilead and later extended his rule “over all Israel.”

10.zh:
掃羅的兒子伊施波設登基的時候年四十歲，作以色列王二年；惟獨猶大家歸從大衛。

兩年。伊施波設與大衛同年開始統治，在瑪哈念統治了兩年。這並不是伊施波設全部的統治時期，而是說在兩年後發生了即將描述的事件：押尼珥與大衛的戰爭（12-32節），掃羅家與大衛家的持久戰（撒下3:1），和押尼珥向大衛倒戈（撒下3:6-39）（見《先祖與先知》699頁）。
10.en: **Two years.** Ish-bosheth began his reign in the same year as David, and reigned two years at Mahanaim. This does not mean that the total length of Ish-bosheth’s reign was two years, but that after two years the events about to be described, Abner’s war with David (vs. 12–32), the long war between the house of Saul and the house of David (ch. 3:1), and Abner’s revolt to David (ch. 3:6–39), took place (see PP 699).

11.zh:
大衛在希伯崙作猶大家的王，共七年零六個月。

**七年零六個月。**這句話似乎是插入語，介紹大衛在希伯侖統治的總年限。我們不知道伊施波設作王的年限（見10節註釋），所以也不知道伊施波設的死和大衛被膏為“以色列的王”的時間間隔（撒下5:3）。
11.en: **Seven years and six months.** This statement seems to be parenthetically introduced to give the total length of David’s reign at Hebron. Since the length of Ish-bosheth’s reign is not known (see on v. 10), we do not know the interval between Ish-bosheth’s death and the time that David was anointed king “over Israel” (ch. 5:3).

12.zh:
尼珥的兒子押尼珥和掃羅的兒子伊施波設的僕人從瑪哈念出來，往基遍去。

**出來。**為了打仗（見撒上18:30；撒下21:17；代上20:1）。
**往基遍去。**押尼珥渴望將他的勢力擴展到全以色列，就冒險來到大衛領地的邊界。基遍在便雅憫境內，在耶路撒冷西北9.2公里，現名ej-Jib。
12.en:
**Went out.** That is, for the purpose of war (see 1 Sam. 18:30; 2 Sam. 21:17; 1 Chron. 20:1).
To Gibeon. Desirous of extending his power over all Israel, Abner ventured to the borders of David’s domain. Gibeon was in the territory of Benjamin, 5 3/4 mi. (9.2 km.) northwest of Jerusalem. The site is now known as ej–Jib.

13.zh:
洗魯雅的兒子約押和大衛的僕人也出來，在基遍池旁與他們相遇；一班坐在池這邊，一班坐在池那邊。

**洗魯雅。**洗魯雅是大衛的姐姐（代上2:16），因此約押就是大衛的外甥。他後來成了大衛軍隊的元帥（代上11:6；參撒下5:8）。
**基遍池。**在基遍山的東南，有一個豐富的泉源流到從石灰石中鑿出的一個蓄水池中。下面還保留著一個大型露天水庫的遺蹟，貯存從其地下的泉源湧出的泉水。約押與押尼珥的軍隊駐紮在池的兩邊，彼此可以望見。
13.en:
**Zeruiah.** Zeruiah was the sister of David (1 Chron. 2:16), and Joab was therefore the nephew of David. He later became the commander in chief of David’s armies (1 Chron. 11:6; cf. 2 Sam. 5:8).
The pool of Gibeon. To the southeast of the hill of Gibeon is a copious spring that issues into a reservoir excavated in the limestone rock. Below, a large open reservoir, the ruins of which still remain, stored the overflow from this subterranean spring. The forces of Joab and Abner sat in full sight of each other, on opposite sides of the pool.

14.zh:
押尼珥對約押說：讓少年人起來，在我們面前戲耍吧！約押說：可以。

**戲耍。**押尼珥向約押挑戰，要從各方中選出的相同數量的戰士進行格鬥來比實力。古時戰前常舉行這樣的格鬥。
14.en: **Play.** Abner challenged Joab to a test of strength to be decided by a combat between an equal number of champions to be selected from each side. Such contests preceding a battle were not uncommon in ancient times.

16.zh:
彼此揪頭，用刀刺肋，一同仆倒。所以，那地叫做希利甲哈素林，就在基遍。

**希利甲哈素林。**一個紀念性的名字，意思是“燧石之地”或“（劍）刃之地”。七十士譯本為“背信棄義之人的那一份”。
16.en: **Helkath-hazzurim.** A commemorative name that means “field of flints” or “field of [sword] edges.” The LXX renders this, “the portion of the treacherous ones.”

17.zh:
那日的戰事兇猛，押尼珥和以色列人敗在大衛的僕人面前。

**戰事兇猛。**參戰的人數可能並不很多，因為大衛一方只有20個人被殺，以色列一方有360人被殺（30,31節），但是這場戰鬥進行得很劇烈，最終給猶大的部隊帶來了決定性的勝利。
17.en: **A very sore battle.** The numbers engaged were probably not large, since the total of those slain was only 20 on the side of David and 360 on the side of Israel (vs. 30, 31), but the contest was fought out with a fierceness that brought a decisive victory to the forces of Judah.

19.zh:
亞撒黑追趕押尼珥，直追趕他不偏左右。

**亞撒黑追趕。**押尼珥是對抗大衛的中堅力量。如果能在這場戰事中除掉他，伊施波設的事業就會崩潰了，整個國家很快就會統一在大衛的領導之下。亞撒黑明白這一點，就對以色列的元帥緊追不捨。
19.en: **Asahel pursued.** Abner was the backbone of the resistance against David. If he could be put out of the contest, the cause of Ish-bosheth would collapse, and the entire kingdom would quickly be united under David. Understanding this, Asahel persistently kept on the heels of Israel’s commander in chief.

21.zh:
押尼珥對他說：你或轉向左轉向右，拿住一個少年人，剝去他的戰衣。亞撒黑卻不肯轉開不追趕他。

**你轉向。**押尼珥認出追趕他的仇敵是約押的兄弟，就不願意傷害他，並勸他到旁邊去與一個較差的對手格鬥。亞撒黑雖然腳快（18節），卻無法對付一個可能比他更強壯老練的戰士。
21.en: **Turn thee aside.** Recognizing that the foe who was pursuing him was the brother of Joab, Abner was unwilling to injure him and urged that he turn aside and content himself with some meaner antagonist. Though light of foot (v. 18), Asahel was no match for a probably more robust and seasoned warrior.

22.zh:
押尼珥又對亞撒黑說：你轉開不追趕我吧！我何必殺你呢？若殺你，有什麼臉見你哥哥約押呢？

**有什麼臉。**押尼珥再次嘗試勸阻亞撒黑追趕他，說明他擔心如果自己殺了大衛勇猛元帥的兄弟，不可避免地會釀成族仇。
22.en: **Hold up my face.** Abner made a second attempt to dissuade Asahel from his pursuit, making it clear that he feared the blood feud that must inevitably follow if he were to slay the brother of David’s doughty commander in chief.

23.zh:
亞撒黑仍不肯轉開。故此，押尼珥就用槍鐏刺入他的肚腹，甚至槍從背後透出，亞撒黑就在那裡仆倒而死。眾人趕到亞撒黑仆倒而死的地方，就都站住。

**肚腹。**第五肋下（見撒下3:27；4:6；20:10）。
23.en: **Under the fifth rib.** This expression (see ch. 3:27; 4:6; 20:10) simply means “abdomen,” and should be so translated.

24.zh:
約押和亞比篩追趕押尼珥，日落的時候，到了通基遍曠野的路旁，基亞對面的亞瑪山。

**亞瑪山。**這個地方和基亞都不確定。
24.en: **The hill of Ammah.** Neither this place nor Giah has been identified.

25.zh:
便雅憫人聚集，跟隨押尼珥站在一個山頂上。

**聚集。**押尼珥的軍隊似乎已經分散了，但是便雅憫人還是在一起，現在跟隨押尼珥站在一個山頂的有利地形上。
25.en: **Gathered themselves.** It appears that Abner’s forces had become widely scattered, but the Benjamites had kept together and now joined Abner in a strong position upon a hilltop.

26.zh:
押尼珥呼叫約押說：刀劍豈可永遠殺人嗎？你豈不知終久必有苦楚嗎？你要等何時才叫百姓回去、不追趕弟兄呢？

豈可永遠殺人嗎？押尼珥的軍隊在戰鬥中損失慘重，但是如果約押繼續進攻，憑著押尼珥軍隊現在所處山頂的有利地形，會給約押的軍隊造成重大傷亡。押尼珥知道自己無法獲勝，也知道約押會曉得要是他決定擊潰處於這個堅固防禦地點的押尼珥的話，會付上重大代價，所以押尼珥就呼籲對方的軍隊停止追擊他們的希伯來同胞。押尼珥曾挑起爭戰，現在他又呼籲和平了。這一呼籲主要是因為他自己的失敗和危險，而不是出於終止與大衛家爭鬥的真誠願望。他求和的提議是由於環境的改變，而不是內心的改變。
26.en: **Devour for ever.** The forces of Abner had lost heavily in the struggle, but in their present hilltop position they would have been able to inflict heavy losses upon the troops of Joab if the latter had persisted in the attack. Knowing that he was in no position to win, and knowing also that Joab would be aware of the heavy price he would have to pay if he was determined to rout him from his strong defensive position, Abner now made an appeal to the opposing forces to stop pursuing their fellow Hebrews. Abner had laid down a challenge to war, and he now set forth an appeal for peace. In this appeal Abner was motivated largely by his own defeat and present danger, and not by a sincere desire to terminate the struggle with the house of David. His conciliatory proposal was dictated by a change in circumstances, not by a change of heart.

27.zh:
約押說：我指著永生的神起誓：你若不說戲耍的那句話，今日早晨百姓就回去，不追趕弟兄了。

**你若不說。**約押這句話的意思不明確。有幾種解釋：（1）約押是指早上的事件，將戰鬥的責任歸到押尼珥身上，並堅持說要不是押尼珥挑戰的話，雙方的人那天早上都準備不作戰就回家的。（2）約押竭力告訴押尼珥，要不是他求和，人們會繼續作戰直到早晨，暗示會給押尼珥造成更大的損失。（3）即使押尼珥不說，約押原來也是想戰鬥到早晨的，但是鑑於押尼珥現在的請求，他願意在此時就停戰。總的來說，約押似乎盡力把責任推押尼珥身上。押尼珥在基遍的魯莽挑戰帶來了弟兄之間當天的戰鬥。參與內戰是極其不幸的。約押設法使自己擺脫對發生之事的責任。
27.en: **Unless thou hadst spoken.** The exact meaning of these words of Joab is not clear. Several interpretations have been offered: (1) Joab is referring back to the events of the morning, placing the blame for the struggle upon Abner and insisting that the people on both sides were ready that morning to go to their homes without a battle had not Abner issued his challenge to war. (2) Joab was endeavoring to make it clear to Abner that had he not asked for peace the people would have continued the struggle till the morning, with all that that implied of still further disastrous results for Abner. (3) Even if Abner had not spoken, Joab had intended continuing the struggle only till the morning, but in view of Abner’s present request he was willing to call off the battle at this juncture. On the whole, it seems that Joab was endeavoring to place the blame upon Abner, whose rash challenge at Gibeon had brought on the struggle that day between brother and brother. To engage in civil war was most unfortunate, and Joab sought to clear himself of responsibility for what had occurred.

28.zh:
於是約押吹角，眾民就站住，不再追趕以色列人，也不再打仗了。

**再。**`od，直譯是“還，”“仍，”“又”。該詞表達繼續的意思，但不一定是無止境的持續。此處為期顯然有限，因為“掃羅家與大衛家爭戰許久”（撒下3:1）。“再”只是標誌著這場戰鬥的結束。
28.en: **Any more.** Heb. ‘od, literally, “still,” “yet,” “again.” The word expresses continuance but not necessarily endless duration. Here the duration is definitely limited, for “there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David” (ch. 3:1). The words “any more” simply mark the termination of this particular war.

29.zh:
押尼珥和跟隨他的人整夜經過亞拉巴，過約但河，走過畢倫，到了瑪哈念。

**整夜經過。**押尼珥無意冒第二天早晨繼續戰鬥的風險，就立即撤退了。
**經過亞拉巴。**或“經過平原”。亞拉巴指約旦盆地，從加利利海到死海，再到從死海南部延伸到亞喀巴灣的盆地。
**畢倫。**詞根是bathar（“切成兩個”）。因此從在一個地區被山與山谷切開的意義上，可能指一個峽谷。畢倫一般認為是通向瑪哈唸的一個不知名的山谷或地區。有人把“切成兩個”的意思用在一天上，認為押尼珥和跟隨他的人在整夜撤退後，又行軍了“整個上午”，即接下來的一天的一半。
29.en:
**Walked all that night.** Abner did not intend to run the risk of continuing the struggle the next morning, but made an immediate withdrawal.
Through the plain. Literally, “through the Arabah.” The Arabah is a term applied to the depression of the Jordan, from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea and to the depression extending south of the Dead Sea to the Gulf of Aqabah.
Bithron. From the root bathar, “to cut in two.” Hence probably a ravine in the sense of a region being cut up with mountains and valley. Bithron has generally been understood as an unknown valley or district leading to Mahanaim. Some apply the idea of “to cut in two” to a day and make Abner and his men continue their all-night retreat by marching in addition “the whole forenoon,” that is, half of the following day (see RSV).

30.zh:
約押追趕押尼珥回來，聚集眾民，見大衛的僕人中缺少了十九個人和亞撒黑。

**十九人。**可能是除了那天早晨死在基遍的12個人之外（15,16節）。
30.en: **Nineteen men.** These were probably in addition to the 12 men who died that morning at Gibeon (vs. 15, 16).

31.zh:
但大衛的僕人殺了便雅憫人和跟隨押尼珥的人，共三百六十名。

**三百六十名。**猶大人與以色列人損失人數的這麼大差異，可能是由於大衛的人是老練的戰士，曾在大衛被掃羅長期追逐期間與他在一起（見撒上23:13；27:2；30:9），而押尼珥的人可能是掃羅失敗後剩下的軍隊。
31.en: **Three hundred and threescore.** This great disparity between the losses among the men of Judah and those of Israel may have been due to the fact that David’s men were seasoned veterans who had been with him in his long period of flight from Saul (see 1 Sam. 23:13; 27:2; 30:9), while Abner’s men were probably remnants of Saul’s defeated army.

32.zh:
眾人將亞撒黑送到伯利恆，葬在他父親的墳墓裡。約押和跟隨他的人走了一夜，天亮的時候到了希伯崙。

**將亞撒黑送到。**被殺的其他士兵可能就埋在他們倒下的地方，但是因為亞撒黑與大衛和約押的關係，他的屍體被帶到了伯利恆，葬在他家的墓地裡。
**天亮的時候。**希伯侖在伯利恆南西南22.4公里，距基遍36.8公里。對大衛的人來說，這是一次不同尋常的壯舉。他們長久追擊了押尼珥的軍隊後，在黃昏後離開戰場（24節），找到亞撒黑的屍體，將它帶到伯利恆，葬在他家的墳地裡，然後繼續行軍在天亮的時候抵達希伯侖。然而沒有明說這次整夜行軍是從戰場還是從伯利恆出發的。可能是從伯利恆出發的，因為埋葬亞撒黑需要一些時間。
有時很難理解人某種行為的動機。這種行為回想起來。似乎是非常愚蠢的。我們只能希望人會作出更好的判斷。
32.en:
**Took up Asahel.** The bodies of the other soldiers who were slain were probably buried where they fell, but because of Asahel’s relationship to both David and Joab his body was taken to Bethlehem, where it was given burial in the family tomb.
At break of day. Hebron was 14 mi. (22.4 km.) south-southwest of Bethlehem and 23 mi. (36.8 km.) from Gibeon. It would have been a remarkable feat for David’s men, after their long pursuit of the forces of Abner, to leave the scene of battle after nightfall (v. 24), secure the body of Asahel, take it to Bethlehem, bury it in the family tomb, and then continue their march to reach Hebron by daybreak. However, the narrative does not make clear whether the overnight march was from the battlefield or from Bethlehem. Perhaps it was from the latter, inasmuch as some time would be involved in the burial of Asahel.
It is sometimes difficult to understand the motives that prompt a man to take a certain course of action that seems, in retrospect, to have been ill-advised. One cannot help but wish that better judgment had prevailed.

1.zh:
掃羅家和大衛家爭戰許久。大衛家日見強盛；掃羅家日見衰弱。

**爭戰許久。**掃羅家與大衛家沒有公開作戰，而是處於敵對狀態，持續了五年左右，因為爭戰開始前伊施波設在瑪哈唸作王二年（撒下2:10），大衛成為“全以色列”的王之前，在希伯侖作王七年零六個月（撒下5:5）。在這段時間，大衛大都讓事態自然發展。他沒有進攻以色列，而是等候事件的結果，相信上帝早先關於賜給他國度的應許必定實現。
**大衛家日漸強盛。**局勢對大衛有利。伊施波設是一個怯懦的人。幾年不稱職的統治，再加上幾年沒有王，使以色列人渴望大衛提供給猶大的積極進取的領導。大衛是一個有個性有才華的人，他的大膽與勇氣使他受到了百姓的愛戴。隨著歲月的流逝，他越來越顯明為耶和華所任命的國家領袖。甚至在掃羅的最後一戰時，都有不少瑪拿西支派的人叛離來歸向大衛，“天天”有人來幫助大衛（代上12:19-22）。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–39節）**。《先祖與先知》第699，700頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–30節）**。《先祖與先知》第699頁。
1.en:
**There was long war.** There was not open warfare but a state of hostility between the houses of Saul and David. This situation must have continued about five years, for Ish-bosheth reigned two years at Mahanaim before war began (ch. 2:10) and David reigned seven years and six months at Hebron before he became king over “all Israel” (ch. 5:5). During this time David was content largely to allow matters to take their own course. Instead of taking the offensive against Israel, David awaited the outcome of events, confident of the early fulfillment of God’s promises to him concerning the kingdom.
David waxed stronger. Time was on David’s side. Ish-bosheth was a weakling, and a few years of incompetent rule, followed by a few more without a king, made Israel long for the type of aggressive leadership that David provided for Judah. David was a man of character and prowess, and his daring and courage had endeared him to the hearts of the people. As the years went by it became increasingly evident that he was the man whom the Lord had ordained for the kingdom. Even on the occasion of Saul’s last battle there had been a significant defection to David from the tribe of Manasseh, with men continuing to come to his side “day by day” (1 Chron. 12:19–22).

2.zh:
大衛在希伯崙得了幾個兒子：長子暗嫩是耶斯列人亞希暖所生的；

**生了幾個兒子。**雖然上帝暫時忍受了多妻的習俗（見申14:26），但祂並沒有阻止這種生活模式的罪惡後果。鬥爭、爭奪、不和、嫉妒與辛酸臨到了大衛的家庭，並給王國的百姓留下了邪惡的影響。大衛在希伯侖生的兒子中，有三個給他、給他的家庭、並給國家帶來了大量的煩惱與災禍。
**暗嫩。**直譯是“信實的。”關於大衛與這個兒子的不幸經歷，見撒下13章。
2.en:
**Sons born.** Though God suffered the practice of polygamy for a time (see on Deut. 14:26), He did not prevent the evil results of such a mode of life. Strife, contention, variance, jealousy, and bitterness came to David’s household and left their evil effects upon the people of the realm. Three of the sons born to David at Hebron brought much vexation and woe to him, to his family, and to the nation.
Amnon. Literally, “faithful.” See ch. 13 for the record of the unhappy experience of David with this son.

3.zh:
次子基利押（在歷代上三章一節作但以利）是作過迦密人拿八的妻亞比該所生的；三子押沙龍是基述王達買的女兒瑪迦所生的；

**基利押（在歷代上三章一節作但以利）。**關於他沒有更多的信息。可能是早逝了。
**押沙龍。**關於這個兒子的不幸歷史，他的謀反與死亡都記錄在撒下13至18章。
**基述。**黑門山腳下的一個地區，在加利利海東面和北面（申3:14；書12:5；13:11,13；代上2:23）。但聖經提到當大衛住在洗革拉時，曾侵奪過住在猶大南部內蓋夫地區的基述人（撒上27:8）。撒下15:8的話似乎確定瑪迦出身的基述是亞蘭的一個地區。
3.en:
**Chileab.** Called “Daniel” in 1 Chron. 3:1. Nothing further is known of him. It is possible that he died at an early age.
Absalom. The sad history of this son, his rebellion, and death are recorded in chs. 13 to 18.
Geshur. An area below Mt. Hermon east and and north of the Sea of Galilee (Deut. 3:14; Joshua 12:5; 13:11, 13; 1 Chron. 2:23). However, there were Geshurites mentioned as living in a district in the Negeb on the south of Judah invaded by David during his residence in Ziklag (1 Sam. 27:8). The statement in 2 Sam. 15:8 seems to identify the Geshur from which Maacah came as a Syrian region.

4.zh:
四子亞多尼雅是哈及所生的；五子示法提雅是亞比他所生的；

**亞多尼雅。**直譯是“耶和華是我的主”。這個兒子在大衛年老時曾企圖篡位（王上1:5），後來被所羅門處死（王上2:24,25）。在三個哥哥，包括基利押死後，亞多尼雅認為自己是合法的王位繼承人。
**示法提雅。**直譯是“耶和華已審判。”關於這個兒子沒有任何信息。
4.en:
**Adonijah.** Literally, “Yahweh is my Lord.” This is the son who, when David was old, aspired to the crown (1 Kings 1:5), and was later put to death by Solomon (1 Kings 2:24, 25). After the death of his three elder brothers, Chileab being presumably dead, Adonijah regarded himself the rightful heir to the throne.
Shephatiah. Literally, “Yahweh has judged.” Nothing is known concerning this son.

5.zh:
六子以特念是大衛的妻以格拉所生的。大衛這六個兒子都是在希伯崙生的。

**以特念，以格拉所生。**關於這個兒子和他的母親沒有任何信息。
**大衛的妻。**按照猶太人的解釋，這個稱呼表示以格拉在大衛的妻中是排行第一的。其他人則認為這種稱呼是應是指前面列出的所有女子。
5.en:
**Ithream, by Eglah.** Nothing is known of this son or his mother.
David’s wife. According to the Jewish interpretation this title is taken to mean that Eglah was first in rank among David’s wives. Others see in the expression a description applying to all the precedingly listed women.

6.zh:
掃羅家和大衛家爭戰的時候，押尼珥在掃羅家大有權勢。

**大有權勢。**押尼珥繼續在掃羅家的事務中扮演日益重要的角色。他是掃羅搖搖欲墜的王朝的中流砥柱，十分了解自己的重要性。要不是押尼珥的力量，伊施波設根本沒有能力獨自保持以色列的王位。
6.en: **Made himself strong.** Abner kept on assuming an increasingly important role in the affairs of the house of Saul. He was the mainstay of Saul’s tottering dynasty, and well realized his own importance. Except for the strength of Abner, Ish-bosheth would never have been able to maintain his hold upon Israel’s throne.

7.zh:
掃羅有一妃嬪，名叫利斯巴，是愛亞的女兒。一日，伊施波設對押尼珥說：你為什麼與我父的妃嬪同房呢？

**利斯巴。**見撒下21:8-11。
為什麼？在東方國家，國王的妃嬪被認為是他繼承者的產業。因此娶前王的女人被視為對王位的主張（見撒下12:8；16:21；王上2:22）。押尼珥即使犯有所指控的罪，聖經也沒有記載他想奪取伊施波設的王位。但是國王卻把所涉的行為看作是背叛，因此惹怒了押尼珥。伊施波設責備的話是可以理解的，因為押尼珥所涉的行為侵犯了國王的權利。
7.en:
**Rizpah.** See ch. 21:8–11.
Wherefore? In Oriental lands the harem of a king was regarded as the property of his successor, and the taking of a woman who had belonged to the previous king was therefore regarded as an assertion of a claim to the throne (see 2 Sam. 12:8; 16:21; 1 Kings 2:22). There is nothing in the record to indicate that Abner, if guilty of the act of which he was charged, had any design on Ish-bosheth’s throne, but the king nevertheless preferred to regard the alleged conduct as an act of treachery, and it was this that aroused the anger of Abner. Ish-bosheth’s words of reproach are understandable, for Abner’s alleged deed violated the rights of the king.

8.zh:
押尼珥因伊施波設的話就甚發怒，說：我豈是猶大的狗頭呢？我恩待你父掃羅的家和他的弟兄、朋友，不將你交在大衛手裡，今日你竟為這婦人責備我嗎？

**甚發怒。**押尼珥很生氣，因為他所支持、需要他輔助才能坐寶座的人竟敢指責他。
**狗頭。**七十士譯本無“猶大的”。押尼珥的話並不是為自己辯護，而是表達對伊施波設責備的不滿。伊施波設可能對押尼珥說了某種責備的話，押尼珥現在反問他是不是這種討厭無用的畜生——他曾對猶大采那麼強硬的立場，並繼續對掃羅家顯示這麼大的仁慈。
8.en:
**Very wroth.** Abner was angry because the one who owed his throne solely to his support now dared to reproach and upbraid him.
Dog’s head. The first part of Abner’s reply reads literally, “Am I a dog’s head which belongs to Judah?” The LXX omits the expression “which belongs to Judah.” Abner’s words were not an attempt to justify himself, but rather an expression of his resentment of Ish-bosheth’s rebuke. Ish-bosheth had probably employed some term of reproach against Abner, and Abner now responded by asking whether after all he was such a vile and worthless creature—he who had taken so strong a position against Judah and had continued to show such great kindness to the house of Saul.

9.zh:
我若不照著耶和華起誓應許大衛的話行，廢去掃羅的位，建立大衛的位，使他治理以色列和猶大，從但直到別是巴，願神重重地降罰與我！併於上節。

**照著耶和華起誓應許的。**這句話表明耶和華揀選大衛繼承掃羅已廣為人知。聖經並沒有記錄上帝起誓要把國給大衛，但是押尼珥顯然明白這個應許就是莊嚴的誓約。這裡可能寓指上帝“必不說謊也不後悔”，藉著撒母耳應許要把國度從掃羅奪回，交給大衛（撒上 15:28,29）。
**廢去掃羅的位。**押尼珥決心把掃羅的國度轉交給大衛可能不是草率決定的。這位元帥也許早就想放棄維持搖搖欲墜的掃羅家族。伊施波設的責備似乎給了他機會實施他已經作出的決定。
**從但直到別示巴。**指整個以色列王國，從最北端到最南端。這個詞組一直在士師時期使用，延續到所羅門的時代（士20:1；撒上3:20；撒下17:11；24:2,15；王上4:25；代上21:2）。但是自從王國分裂以後，該詞組只用過一次，就是西希家邀請“從別示巴直到但”以色列全家的時候（代下30:5），為要共同慶祝逾越節。
**願上帝重重地降罰與我。**這是嚴肅起誓的語言（見路1:17；撒上3:17；25:22；撒下19:13；王上19:2；王下6:31）。押尼珥發誓要把國給大衛；如果他不說到做到，願上帝的憤怒臨到自己。
9.en:
**So do God to Abner.** These words are in the form of a solemn oath (see Ruth 1:17; 1 Sam. 3:17; 25:22; 2 Sam. 19:13; 1 Kings 19:2; 2 Kings 6:31). Abner swears that he will transfer the kingdom to David, and invokes the wrath of God upon himself if he does not fulfill his word.
As the Lord hath sworn. This statement shows how generally it was known that the Lord had chosen David to succeed Saul. There is no record of an oath on the part of God to deliver the kingdom to David, but Abner evidently understood the promise as solemnly sworn. Perhaps there is an allusion to the words “will not lie nor repent” as regards the promise God made through Samuel to rend the kingdom from Saul and to give it to David (1 Sam. 15:28, 29).

11.zh:
伊施波設懼怕押尼珥，不敢回答一句。

**懼怕押尼珥。**這節經文清楚地指出了伊施波設政權的真實性質。這位軟弱的國王懼怕回答押尼珥，因為知道這個人握有寶座背後的實權。
11.en: **Feared him.** This verse points out clearly the real nature of Ish-bosheth’s government. The weak king was afraid to make a reply to the man he knew to be the real power behind the throne.

12.zh:
押尼珥打發人去見大衛，替他說：這國歸誰呢？又說：你與我立約，我必幫助你，使以色列人都歸服你。

**替他說。**直譯是“他所在的地方”。七十士譯本的盧西安修訂本為“到希伯侖。”
這國歸誰呢？押尼珥意識到自己正在與大衛進行交易。他希望有條件地把國交給大衛，那就是大衛要與他立約，並明確保證對他作適當考慮。在這個建議中，押尼珥狹窄、傲慢、自私自利的精神暴露無遺。他願意把命運交給大衛，但有一個要價，並要首先確定這個要價會得到支付。
12.en:
**On his behalf.** Literally, “where he was.” The Lucian edition of the LXX reads “to Hebron.”
Whose is the land? Abner recognized that he was in a position to bargain with David. He would bring about the transfer of the land on one condition, that David make a league with him, giving him definite assurance of proper consideration for himself. In this proposal the narrow, haughty, self-seeking spirit of Abner was clearly revealed. He would throw in his lot with David, but only at a price, and he wanted first to make certain that the price would be paid.

13.zh:
大衛說：好！我與你立約。但有一件，你來見我面的時候，若不將掃羅的女兒米甲帶來，必不得見我的面。

**將米甲帶來。**掃羅曾把米甲嫁給大衛（撒上18:20,21,27），所以米甲當然是屬於他的。但是大衛的要求除了正義問題之外，也帶有政治性目的，因為掃羅的女兒作為猶大的王后對掃羅的部屬是有影響的。這說明大衛對掃羅的家並沒有惡意，並且大衛作為前國王女婿的身份，對於王國的權利會得到進一步的加強。
13.en: **Bring Michal.** Michal had been given to David by Saul (1 Sam. 18:20, 21, 27) and was rightfully his. But besides the question of the justice of David’s demand was the politic consideration of the effect on Saul’s partisans of having a daughter of Saul as queen of Judah. This would tend to show that David had no malice against the house of Saul, and David’s right to the kingdom would be further enhanced by his being the son-in-law of the previous king.

14.zh:
大衛就打發人去見掃羅的兒子伊施波設，說：你要將我的妻米甲歸還我；他是我從前用一百非利士人的陽皮所聘定的。

**去見……伊施波設。**派使者去見伊施波設而不是去見押尼珥，可能是因為當時押尼珥與大衛的談判是秘密進行的。另一方面，也應該是右伊施波設作為國王發令歸還米甲。沒有押尼珥的支持，伊施波設就無法抗拒大衛的要求。遵行那個要求，表明了伊施波設的軟弱，表明他承認大衛受了虧待，並承認大衛的要求是正當的。伊施波設開接受這個要求，就向所有猶大和以色列的人表明他的日子屈指可數了，不久大衛就會接管整個王國。
**一百……陽皮。**掃羅要求100陽皮，但大衛給了200（撒上18:25,27）。
14.en:
**To Ish-bosheth.** The messengers were sent to Ish-bosheth and not to Abner, probably because the negotiations between Abner and David were then still secret. On the other hand it was Ish-bosheth who as king would have to issue the orders for Michal’s return. Without the support of Abner, Ish-bosheth would be in no position to resist David’s demand. In complying with that demand, Ish-bosheth would reveal his own weakness, acknowledge the wrong that had been done to David, and the justice of David’s demand. For Ish-bosheth publicly to accede to this demand would give evidence to all in both Judah and Israel that his days were numbered and that David would soon take over the entire kingdom.
An hundred foreskins. Saul had demanded 100 foreskins but 200 had been delivered (1 Sam. 18:25, 27).

15.zh:
伊施波設就打發人去，將米甲從拉億的兒子、他丈夫帕鐵那裡接回來。

**帕鐵。**他家住在迦琳（撒上25:44）。據賽10:29,30，迦琳似乎離基比亞和亞拿突不遠。但是他可能已遷居到約旦河對岸的瑪哈念地區，和掃羅的支持者在一起。
15.en: **Phaltiel.** Or “Phalti,” whose home was in Gallim (1 Sam. 25:44), which, according to Isa. 10:29, 30, seems to have been not far from Gibeah and Anathoth. But he had probably taken up his residence across the Jordan in the region of Mahanaim with the adherents of Saul.

16.zh:
米甲的丈夫跟著他，一面走一面哭，直跟到巴戶琳。押尼珥說：你回去吧！帕鐵就回去了。

**在她後面哭。**這個感人的畫面可能值得同情，但是應該記住，帕鐵以別人的妻子為妻是不對的。
**巴戶琳。**據認為是Râs et-Tmîm，在斯高帕斯山的東邊，耶路撒冷的正東北。
**押尼珥說。**這句話表明歸還米甲的談判是押尼珥負責的。這件事關係重大，顯然由押尼珥親自掌管。
16.en:
**Weeping behind her.** The sentence may be rendered more smoothly, “And her husband went with her, weeping as he walked behind her.” Though sympathy may be evoked by this touching tale it should be borne in mind that Phaltiel had erred in taking another man’s wife to himself.
Bahurim. Thought to be Râs eṭ–Ṭmîm, east of Mt. Scopus, just northeast of Jerusalem.
Then said Abner. These words indicate that the negotiations for the return of Michal were in the hands of Abner. This being a matter of such vital importance, Abner evidently took personal charge.

17.zh:
押尼珥對以色列長老說：從前你們願意大衛作王治理你們，

**你們願意大衛作王。**這句話暗示掃羅死在基利波之後，可能有一場群眾運動，要立大衛作全以色列的王。當時押尼珥反對這種要求。現在他改變了方針，就精明地提醒長老們他所建議的實際上就是他們的意見。對於押尼珥來說，在迫近的步驟中，必須獲得這些重要官員的同意與合作。
17.en: **Ye sought for David.** These words suggest that there may have been a popular movement, after the death of Saul at Gilboa, to have David established as king over all Israel. At the time Abner was opposed to such a demand. Now, with his change in policy, he prudently reminded the elders that what he was recommending was really their suggestion. It was essential for Abner to secure the consent and cooperation of these prominent officials in the impending moves.

18.zh:
現在你們可以照心願而行。因為耶和華曾論到大衛說：我必藉我僕人大衛的手，救我民以色列脫離非利士人和眾仇敵的手。

**耶和華曾論到大衛說。**這句話無疑是真實的，但是聖經裡沒有與這句話的意思完全相同的句子。這句話可能是藉著一位先知說的，如撒母耳、迦得或拿單。但這幾位先知的語只保存了很小一部分。
18.en: **The Lord hath spoken.** This statement is undoubtedly true, but no exact words to this effect have come down to us in the Biblical record. The pronouncement was probably made through one of the prophets, Samuel, Gad, or Nathan, but only a very small percentage of the words of the prophets have been preserved.

19.zh:
押尼珥也用這話說給便雅憫人聽，又到希伯崙，將以色列人和便雅憫全家一切所喜悅的事說給大衛聽。

**便雅憫人。**掃羅是便雅憫支派的。與這個支派的人協商時需要特別小心。他們與掃羅有血親關係，並曾因這種關係而享受很大的利益。押尼珥親自去與便雅憫人協商，就像他在希伯侖與大衛協商一樣。
19.en: **Of Benjamin.** Saul was of the tribe of Benjamin. Particular care would be necessary in the negotiations with the adherents of that tribe. They felt bound to Saul by ties of kinship and had enjoyed great advantages by virtue of their connection with him. Abner went in person to carry on his negotiations with Benjamin as he did also with David at Hebron.

21.zh:
押尼珥對大衛說：我要起身去招聚以色列眾人來見我主我王，與你立約，你就可以照著心願作王。於是大衛送押尼珥去，押尼珥就平平安安地去了。

**押尼珥就平平安安地去了。**條款既已商定，盟約就嚴肅地獲得批准。押尼珥回來準備執行合約了。
21.en: **He went in peace.** The terms having been agreed upon the league solemnly ratified, Abner returned ready to carry out his part of the compact.

22.zh:
約押和大衛的僕人攻擊敵軍，帶回許多的掠物。那時押尼珥不在希伯崙大衛那裡，因大衛已經送他去，他也平平安安地去了。

**攻擊敵軍。**gedud，通常指“一支劫匪”，“一支軍隊”，但這裡似乎是指“一次突襲”或“一次奇襲”。這次的突襲可能是針對亞瑪力人、非利士人或其他猶大的敵人。這次出征是大衛計劃的，所以在押尼珥來訪時，約押並不在場。約押回來了，因他的勝利和大量的戰利品而興高采烈。
**不在大衛那裡。**這句話緊接在約押回來之後，暗示押尼珥在約押回來之前離開不僅僅是一個巧合。因為這兩個對抗的將軍當時面對面相遇可能會毀了所有和平的前景。
22.en:
**Pursuing a troop.** Heb. gedud, which generally means “a marauding band,” “a troop,” but here seems to be used in the sense of “a foray,” or “a raid.” The sentence should read, “Joab came from a foray.” The raid had probably been against the Amalekites, the Philistines, or some other enemy of Judah. It is possible that the expedition had been planned by David, so that Joab would not be present during Abner’s visit. Joab returned, elated with his victory and the great spoil.
Not with David. The introduction of this item immediately after the mention of Joab’s return, suggests that the departure of Abner before Joab’s return was more than a mere coincidence. For the two rival generals to meet face to face at that juncture might have ruined all prospects of peace.

24.zh:
約押去見王說：你這是做什麼呢？押尼珥來見你，你為何送他去，他就蹤影不見了呢？

你這是作什麼呢？約押強烈反對大衛秘密與押尼珥協商。約押可能真的懷疑押尼珥的誠意，另外還帶有一種私人的恩怨，部分是由於在這個著名的老戰士身上，約押發現了一個強大的對手，部分是由於他與押尼珥之間因亞撒黑被殺而結下的血仇（撒下2:22,23）。
24.en: What hast thou done? Joab bitterly remonstrated with David for having secretly negotiated with Abner. Joab may have had an honest suspicion of Abner’s integrity, but in addition there existed a feeling of personal enmity, due partly to the fact that in the famous old warrior Joab would find a formidable rival, and partly to the blood feud between him and Abner for the slaying of Asahel (2 Sam. 2:22, 23).

26.zh:
約押從大衛那裡出來，就打發人去追趕押尼珥，在西拉井追上他，將他帶回來，大衛卻不知道。

**打發人去。**大衛雖不知道，但可能是以他的名義做的。
**西拉井。**或“西拉蓄水池”，位置不確定。有人認為它是`Ain Sārah，在希伯侖北邊約2.4公里。可是這個地方有點不像，因為在這種情況下，押尼珥就會是在約押到達時剛剛離開希伯侖的。有人認為它是Sîret el-Bella`，希伯侖北邊4.3公里的一個山頂，那裡可以看到一個塔的遺蹟。
26.en:
**Sent messengers.** Without the knowledge but probably in the name of David.
Well of Sirah. Or “cistern of Sirah.” The location of this well is not positively known. Some have identified it with ‘Ain Sārah, about 1 1/2 mi. (2.4 km.) north of Hebron. The site seems somewhat unlikely, for in such a case Abner would have just left Hebron when Joab arrived. Others have identified it with Ṣîret el–Bella‘, a mountaintop 2.7 mi. (4.3 km.) north of Hebron, where the ruins of a tower are to be seen.

27.zh:
押尼珥回到希伯崙，約押領他到城門的甕洞，假作要與他說機密話，就在那裡刺透他的肚腹，他便死了。這是報殺他兄弟亞撒黑的仇。

**到城門。**東方國家的城門口是公眾聚會的地方。為了達到目的，約押必須在押尼珥到大衛那裡之前見到押尼珥。
**報他兄弟亞撒黑的仇。**約押為報血仇殺了押尼珥。他可能根據民35:26,27的規定為自己的復仇辯護。值得注意的是，希伯侖是一座逃城（書20:7）。有鑑於此，約押可能在城門口就完成了殺戮。然而亞撒黑是死在戰場上的，而且押尼珥是在不情願和自衛的情況下殺死他的。約押可能不瞭解這些細節。但是他本應該考慮一下自己這種行為的深遠影響。因為這將使國家的統一耽擱一段時間。押尼珥非常相信大衛，似乎沒有起一點疑心。
27.en:
**In the gate.** A city gate in Oriental lands is a common meeting place. To carry out his purpose it was necessary for Joab to meet Abner before Abner reached David.
For the blood of Asahel. Joab slew Abner for blood revenge. He may have justified his retaliation by the provision of Num. 35:26, 27. Interestingly enough, Hebron was a city of refuge (Joshua 20:7) and in view of that fact, Joab may have carried out his deed in the city gate. The death of Asahel, however, took place in battle, and the slaying was an unwilling and reluctant act of self-defense on the part of Abner. Joab may not have been familiar with these details. But he should have studied the far-reaching effect of his deed, delaying as it did the formation of a united kingdom for some time. So great was Abner’s confidence in David that he appears to have had no suspicions.

28.zh:
大衛聽見了，就說：流尼珥的兒子押尼珥的血，這罪在耶和華面前必永不歸我和我的國。

**這罪不歸我和我的國。**大衛有守信用的好名聲，但是殺害押尼珥使他的好名聲受到了損害。他儘量開脫自己在這件事上的責任。
28.en: **Guiltless.** David had the reputation of being a man of his word, but the murder of Abner placed his good name in jeopardy. He did everything possible to absolve himself of any blame in the matter.

29.zh:
願流他血的罪歸到約押頭上和他父的全家；又願約押家不斷有患漏症的，長大痲瘋的，架柺而行的，被刀殺死的，缺乏飲食的。

**願罪歸到。**直譯是“願它旋轉（或轉到）”。大衛在這裡對約押個人復仇的卑鄙行為進行咒詛。咒詛顯示了大衛敏銳的正義感和他對個人卑鄙罪行的義憤。大衛顯然已吩咐不可侵犯押尼珥的人身。約押的行為使人懷疑大衛的正直。大衛想要眾人都知道他與這種背信棄義的行為一點關係都沒有，而且他全心痛恨這種有損於榮譽的事。
**他父的全家。**約押的兄弟亞比篩也參加了殺害押尼珥的陰謀（30節），因此也包括在這一咒詛之中。這個詛咒不只包括這兩個人，還包括他們的後代。古時的民事刑罰似乎常常不只包括直接與罪行的人。對亞幹所犯之罪的刑罰臨到了他全家（書7:22-26）。照樣，在臨到可拉、大坍和亞比蘭的懲罰中，不僅他們滅亡了，他們的妻子和大坍與亞比蘭的孩子們也滅亡了（民16:27-33；另見王下5:27）。有時孩子們可能與他們父母的罪有密切的關係（見書7:15）。還有的時候無辜的孩子因他們的長輩的頑梗而遭受死亡（見民16:27）。在目前這個例子中，我們不知道大衛宣佈的這個咒詛是不是出於靈感，因此它是不是具有效力，或者在大衛對這種行為表達的極度惱怒之外還有什麼意圖，都不得而知。
**漏症。**見利15:2。
**架拐而行的。**有人譯為：“拿紡紗杆的人”，因而指一種女人氣的人，只適合做女人的工作。
**被刀殺死。**或“死在刀上”。
29.en:
**Let it rest.** Literally, “let it whirl [or, whirl about].” David here invokes a curse on Joab for his mean act of seeking personal revenge. The imprecation reveals David’s keen sense of justice and his bitter indignation against an individual guilty of so dastardly a deed. David had evidently given his word that the person of Abner would be inviolate. The action of Joab cast suspicion on David’s integrity. David wanted all to know that he had had no part in this perfidious deed and that he abhorred with all his soul such a violation of honor.
Father’s house. Abishai, Joab’s brother, had also taken part in the plot to assassinate Abner (v. 30); hence, he too was included in the curse. The imprecation went beyond these two men, to include their posterity. Ancient civil penalties often seem to involve more than those directly connected with the crime. The penalty for Achan’s sin fell upon his whole family (Joshua 7:22–26). Likewise in the judgment upon Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, not only they perished, but their wives and the children of Dathan and Abiram (Num. 16:27–33; see also 2 Kings 5:27). At times the children may have been involved in the crime of their parents (see on Joshua 7:15). At other times innocent children suffered for the obstinacy of their elders (see on Num. 16:27). In the present instance we do not know whether the curse pronounced by David was spoken under inspiration and hence whether it had any validity or any purpose beyond expressing David’s extreme vexation at the deed.
An issue. See Lev. 15:2.
Leaneth on a staff. Some translate, “a distaff holder,” and thus indicate an effeminate person fit only to do a woman’s work.
On the sword. Literally, “by a sword.”

30.zh:
約押和他兄弟亞比篩殺了押尼珥，是因押尼珥在基遍爭戰的時候殺了他們的兄弟亞撒黑。

**約押和亞比篩。**雖然沒有提到亞比篩參與這場陰謀，但這句話暗示在殺死押尼珥這件事上，亞比篩是他兄弟約押的自願幫兇，因此必須分擔所犯罪行的責任。全部行動顯然是有預謀的。
30.en: **Joab and Abishai.** Though nothing is said of Abishai’s part in the plot, this statement implies that Abishai was a willing accomplice with his brother Joab in the slaying of Abner, and thus he too must share his responsibility for the crime committed. The whole act was obviously premeditated.

31.zh:
大衛吩咐約押和跟隨他的眾人說：你們當撕裂衣服，腰束麻布，在押尼珥棺前哀哭。大衛王也跟在棺後。

**腰束麻布。**約押必須通過參加公眾的哀悼，公開譴責自己的罪行。大衛作為喪主親自跟在棺後，顯然穿著王服，因為這裡特別稱他為“大衛王”。
**懷愛倫註釋（31–39節）**。《先祖與先知》第700頁。
31.en: **Gird you with sackcloth.** Joab was required publicly to condemn his own deed by his part in the public mourning. David himself followed the bier as the chief mourner, and evidently dressed in royal attire, for he is here specifically called “king David.”

32.zh:
他們將押尼珥葬在希伯崙。王在押尼珥的墓旁放聲而哭，眾民也都哭了。

**在希伯侖。**這是又一個尊榮和敬重的表示，因為希伯侖是猶大的首都。押尼珥在便雅憫的家本是正常的埋葬之所，但是葬在王城希伯侖會更加光榮。大衛下令將押尼珥葬在首都，有助於使國民相信他對這位被殺的將軍絲毫沒有惡意，還選擇以隆重的方式紀念他。
32.en: **In Hebron.** This was another token of honor and respect, since Hebron was the capital of Judah. Abner’s home in Benjamin would have been the natural burial place, but to the buried in the royal city of Hebron would be more honorable. By ordering the burial of Abner at his capital David would help to convince the nation that he harbored no ill feelings against the slain general and that he chose to honor his memory.

33.zh:
王為押尼珥舉哀，說：押尼珥何竟像愚頑人死呢？

**王為押尼珥舉哀。**在這首簡要、動人而又雄辯的輓歌中，大衛表達了他的悲痛並給予一個倒下的仇敵相稱的頌詞。
33.en: **The king lamented.** In a brief but touching and eloquent elegy David expressed his grief and paid a worthy tribute to a fallen foe.

34.zh:
你手未曾捆綁，腳未曾鎖住。你死，如人死在罪孽之輩手下一樣。於是眾民又為押尼珥哀哭。

**死在罪孽之輩手下。**大衛獻給押尼珥的輓歌是對謀殺以色列元帥兩個兇手的嚴厲譴責。他公開表達了對做出如此卑汙行為之人的輕蔑與鄙視。他讚譽不久前還是他苦毒仇敵的優點所顯示的雅量，贏得了以色列眾人的心（見《先祖與先知》700頁）。百姓知道有象大衛這樣的人在寶座上，國家就處在一個有勇有德，恩威兼施的人掌管之下。
34.en: **Before wicked men.** David’s elegy to Abner was a cutting rebuke to the murderers of Israel’s commander in chief. He publicly expressed his contempt and scorn for men who would perform so foul a deed. His magnanimous recognition of the merits of one who only a short time before had been his bitter enemy won the hearts of all Israel (see PP 700). The people knew that with a man like David on the throne the kingdom would be in the hands of a man with a conscience as well as courage, and with a heart as well as a sword.

35.zh:
日頭未落的時候，眾民來勸大衛吃飯，但大衛起誓說：我若在日頭未落以前吃飯，或吃別物，願神重重地降罰與我！

**日頭未落以前。**禁食直到傍晚是極度悲傷的表示（撒下1:12）。在這日結束前，大衛被百姓力勸中止禁食去進食，但是他斷然拒絕了。他的拒食給百姓留下了深刻而有利的印象。
35.en: **Till the sun be down.** To fast till evening was a sign of deep mourning (ch. 1:12). Before the day was over David was urged by the people to break his fast and to partake of food, but he positively declined. His refusal made a deep and favorable impression upon the people.

38.zh:
王對臣僕說：你們豈不知今日以色列人中死了一個作元帥的大丈夫嗎？

**元帥。**在某些方面，押尼珥是一個具有傑出才幹的人，並且在以色列被視為一個大人物。然而他與大衛立約雖然出於誠意，卻是被自私的動機所驅使。他之所以轉向大衛是想放棄一個註定失敗的事業，併為自己贏得新的尊貴與榮耀。他希望在侍奉大衛中得到最好的地位，但是他的野心，自私和缺乏對上帝的獻身都不利於大衛的國度或上帝的事業。押尼珥的死對於猶大國是一個化裝了的福氣（見《先祖與先知》700頁）。
38.en: **A prince.** In some respects Abner was a man of outstanding ability and would be regarded as a great man in Israel. Yet though sincere in his pact with David, he had been moved by selfish motives. In going over to David he thought to forsake a cause that was doomed and to win new honor and glory to himself. He would have wanted the highest position in the service of David, but his ambition, selfishness, and lack of consecration to God would not have served the best interests of David’s kingdom or the cause of the Lord. Abner’s death was to the kingdom of Judah a blessing in disguise (see PP 700).

39.zh:
我雖然受膏為王，今日還是軟弱；這洗魯雅的兩個兒子比我剛強。願耶和華照著惡人所行的惡報應他。

**我今日還是軟弱。**約押的力量與影響就是大衛的軟弱。如果大衛能做得到的話，他會立即處罰約押，但目前那是不可能的。他現在還不敢嘗試主持正義，免得約押握有的大權和帶軍的聲望引起全面的叛亂。大衛的手是被束縛著的，他向他最親密的朋友坦率地承認了自己的軟弱。
39.en: **I am this day weak.** The strength and influence of Joab was the weakness of David. If he could have done so, David would immediately have punished Joab, but for the present that was not possible. He dared not attempt justice now lest Joab’s great power and popularity with the army cause a general uprising. David’s hands were tied, and to his closest friends he frankly confessed his weakness.

3.10:
**Translate the kingdom.** Abner’s resolve to transfer the kingdom of Saul to David was probably not the result of hasty judgment. The commander may long have pondered the advisability of giving up the attempt to maintain the tottering house of Saul. The rebuke of Ish-bosheth seemed to provide the opportunity to carry into execution a decision that he had previously arrived at.
From Dan even to Beer-sheba. This expression betokens the entire realm of Israel, from its northern to its southern limits. The phrase was used during the period of the judges and up to the time of Solomon (Judges 20:1; 1 Sam. 3:20; 2 Sam. 17:11; 24:2, 15; 1 Kings 4:25; 1 Chron. 21:2), but was employed only once after the division of the monarchy, when Hezekiah sent an invitation to all Israel “from Beer-sheba even to Dan” (2 Chron. 30:5), to unite in the celebration of the Passover.

1.zh:
掃羅的兒子伊施波設聽見押尼珥死在希伯崙，手就發軟；以色列眾人也都驚惶。

**手就發軟。**押尼珥一死，伊施波設的力量就沒有了。王知道他的事業註定失敗。以色列人也都驚惶，因為押尼珥一直是掌握實權的人。他們明白除掉伊施波設、由大衛來接管國家只是時間問題了。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–12節）**。《先祖與先知》第700，701頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第700頁。
1.en: **His hands were feeble.** When Abner died the strength of Ish-bosheth was gone, and the king knew that his cause was doomed. The men of Israel were troubled, because Abner had been the strong hand at the helm. They knew that it was now probably only a question of time before Ish-bosheth would be eliminated and David would take over the kingdom.

2.zh:
掃羅的兒子伊施波設有兩個軍長，一名巴拿，一名利甲，是便雅憫支派、比錄人臨門的兒子。比錄也屬便雅憫。

**軍。**gedudim，“搶劫隊”（見撒下3:22註釋）。
**比錄人。**比錄是基遍的一座城（書9:17），分配給便雅憫支派（書18:25）。一般認為在el-Bīreh附近，在耶路撒冷以北約16公里。
2.en:
**Bands.** Heb. gedudim, “marauding bands” (see on ch. 3:22).
A Beerothite. Beeroth was a Gibeonite city (Joshua 9:17) allocated to the tribe of Benjamin (Joshua 18:25). It is generally sought in the neighborhood of el–Bīreh, about 10 mi. (16 km.) to the north of Jerusalem.

3.zh:
比錄人早先逃到基他音，在那裡寄居，直到今日。

**基他音。**直譯是“兩個迦特”或“兩個酒榨”。基他音的確切地點不詳。便雅憫人被擄到巴比倫歸來之後住在這座城裡（尼11:33）。比錄人逃走可能發生在掃羅殘酷攻擊基遍人的時候（撒下21:1,2）。若是這樣，基他音可能在掃羅統治的地區之外。
3.en: **Gittaim.** Literally, “two Gaths,” or “two wine presses.” The exact site of Gittaim is not known. The city was inhabited by Benjamites after the return from Babylonian exile (Neh. 11:33). The time when the Beerothites fled might have been on the occasion Saul made his cruel attack upon the Gibeonites (2 Sam. 21:1, 2). If that were the case, then Gittaim was probably somewhere outside the domain of Saul.

4.zh:
掃羅的兒子約拿單有一個兒子名叫米非波設，是瘸腿的。掃羅和約拿單死亡的消息從耶斯列傳到的時候，他才五歲。他乳母抱著他逃跑；因為跑得太急，孩子掉在地上，腿就瘸了。

**有一個兒子是瘸腿的。**敘述到這裡似乎中斷了。介紹約拿單兒子的這件事，是要說明掃羅家當時因伊施波設的死幾乎滅絕了。約拿單的兒子似乎是唯一王位的繼承人。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第713頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–12節）**。《先祖與先知》第701頁。
4.en: **A son that was lame.** There seems to be a break here in the narrative. The reason for the introduction of this incident regarding the son of Jonathan is to show that the line of Saul at this time became practically extinct with the death of Ish-bosheth. Jonathan’s son seems to have been the only other candidate for the throne.

5.zh:
一日，比錄人臨門的兩個兒子利甲和巴拿出去，約在午熱的時候到了伊施波設的家；伊施波設正睡午覺。

**午覺。**他正在午休。許多東方國家有午休的習慣。
5.en: **At noon.** He was taking his noonday rest. This is a regular custom in many Oriental lands.

6.zh:
他們進了房子，假作要取麥子，就刺透伊施波設的肚腹，逃跑了。

**取麥子。**這句話各種版本有不同的譯法。七十士譯本為：“看那，這家的（女）守門人揚淨了麥子，打盹睡著了。”拉丁文武加大譯本也說過失在守門的婦人。亞蘭文譯本沒有提麥子。
6.en: **Fetched wheat.** This part of the narrative is rendered variously in the versions. The LXX reads, “And, behold, the porter [feminine] of the house winnowed wheat, and she slumbered and slept.” The Vulgate also lays the blame on the woman who kept the door. The Syriac says nothing about wheat.

7.zh:
他們進房子的時候，伊施波設正在臥房裡躺在床上，他們將他殺死，割了他的首級，拿著首級在亞拉巴走了一夜，

**拿著首級。**他們的目的是把首級帶給大衛，作為伊施波設已死的確據。伊施波設是在中午被殺的（5節），所以刺客們必是在白天把他的首級帶走。要是他們這樣攜帶的話，首級可能裝在一個麥袋裡（見6節）。
**在亞拉巴。**即經過平原，或約旦河流域。
7.en:
**Took his head.** Their purpose was to take the head to David as evidence that Ish-bosheth was certainly dead. Since it was noon when Ish-bosheth was slain (v. 5), the assassins must have carried his head away in daylight. The head may have been placed in one of the wheat sacks, if such they were carrying (see v. 6).
Through the plain. That is, through the Arabah, or valley of the Jordan.

8.zh:
將伊施波設的首級拿到希伯崙見大衛王，說：王的仇敵掃羅曾尋索王的性命。看哪，這是他兒子伊施波設的首級；耶和華今日為我主我王在掃羅和他後裔的身上報了仇。

**曾尋索王的性命。**這兩個軍長可能在掃羅搜索大衛的部隊中扮演了積極的角色。他們可能認為大衛對掃羅和掃羅的家懷有敵意與憎恨，就像掃羅對待大衛那樣。憎恨通常會招惹憎恨；苦毒常常會遭遇苦毒。
**耶和華……報了仇。**尊榮上帝和維護神聖的事業不是這兩個刺客的動機。他們刺殺伊施波設是為謀取自己的私利，並不是為大衛的益處。他們說的話是想讓大衛感激他們，從而獲得優厚的獎賞。這兩個人犯的罪應受到懲罰而不是獎賞。
8.en:
**Which sought thy life.** These captains had probably played an active part with the army of Saul in seeking David’s life, and they may have felt that there was within his heart a similar spirit of enmity and hatred toward Saul and his house as there had been on the part of Saul toward David. Hate usually begets hate, and bitterness on the part of one is often met by bitterness on the part of another.
The Lord hath avenged. The honor of God and the vindication of the divine cause was not the motive that prompted these assassins. They slew Ish-bosheth because they sought their own interests, not the good of David, and their words were calculated to awaken in him a spirit of gratitude toward themselves, that they might receive a handsome reward. The men were guilty of a crime that merited punishment, not reward.

9.zh:
大衛對比錄人臨門的兒子利甲和他兄弟巴拿說：我指著救我性命脫離一切苦難、永生的耶和華起誓：

**救我性命。**大衛十分熟悉上帝和祂公義正直的道路。耶和華曾屢次介入拯救了大衛的性命，挫敗他的仇敵。大衛樂於把復仇留給耶和華（申32:35；參羅12:19；來10:30）。他不需要人的罪行幫助他脫離困難。
9.en: **Redeemed my soul.** David had become well acquainted with God and His ways of justice and right. Repeatedly the Lord had intervened to spare the life of David and to bring distress upon his enemies. David was willing to leave vengeance with the Lord (Deut. 32:35; cf. Rom. 12:19; Heb. 10:30). He did not need the crimes of men to help him out of his troubles.

10.zh:
從前有人報告我說，掃羅死了，他自以為報好消息；我就拿住他，將他殺在洗革拉，這就作了他報消息的賞賜。

**將他殺在。**參撒下1:2-16。
10.en: **And slew him.** The clause thus introduced may be translated, “And I slew him in Ziklag, which was the reward I gave to him for his tidings” (see RSV; cf. ch. 1:2–16).

11.zh:
何況惡人將義人殺在他的床上，我豈不向你們討流他血的罪、從世上除滅你們呢？

**義人。**這句話不是對伊施波設道德品質的全面評價，只是說這個王的品格沒有犯該死的罪。
**討流他血的罪。**大衛對兇手們提一個問題。他把事實的真相擺在他們面前，讓他們自己判斷他的決定是對還是錯。問題只有一個答案，就連被定罪的人也是這樣回答的。公義要求執行死刑。被告沒有什麼話可以辯護的。
許多人處在大衛位置，卻不象大衛這樣思路清楚判斷明智。他們可能認為這兩個刺客是真正的愛國者是，可敬的公民和朋友。他們把謀殺解釋為正義和必要之舉，是為了國家的最高利益。兇手自己也希望這樣解釋他們的行為。但是大衛看透了外表的偽裝，準確地探知他們自私邪惡的動機。既然謀殺符合他們個人的利益，他們就毫不猶豫地去做了。他們假裝是大衛的朋友，但是通過背叛他們所侍奉的人，他們證明自己不配做以色列國的公民。只要形勢的變化使大衛處於不利的情形，他們就會毫不猶豫地殺死他就像殺死伊施波設一樣。這種人是靠不住的。他們不配活著。他們默不作聲，就是向國民宣佈，他們認為對自己的判決是公正的。
**除滅你們。**ba`ar這裡指除去罪惡（申19:13,19等）。兇手的罪行汙穢了大地，只有通過流他們血才能補償，因他們流了無辜之人的血（民35:33）。
11.en:
**A righteous person.** This statement is not intended to be a complete evaluation of Ish-bosheth’s moral character but simply a pronouncement clearing the character of the king from crime worthy of death.
Require his blood. David was addressing a question to the murderers. He had presented the facts before them exactly as they were, and they themselves were to judge whether his decision was right or wrong. There could be only one answer, even from the condemned—they were guilty and were worthy to die. Justice demanded that the sentence of death be executed, and the accused had nothing to say in self-defense.
Many men placed in David’s position would not have thought as clearly or judged as wisely as did David. They might have considered these murderers as true patriots, worthy citizens, and friends. What actually was murder they might have interpreted as a deed of justice and necessity, performed in the best interests of the state. The murderers themselves hoped and certainly expected to have their deed interpreted in that way. But David saw beneath the outward sham, ascertaining correctly their selfish, evil motives. They did not hesitate at murder if it would serve their personal interests. They pretended to be friends of David, but in being traitors to the man they served, they proved themselves to be unworthy citizens of the nation of Israel. Let some turn of events place David in an unfavorable situation, and they would not hesitate to slay him exactly as they had slain Ish-bosheth. Such men could not be trusted. They were not worthy to live, and by their silence they proclaimed to the nation that they regarded the sentence against them as just.
Take you away. Literally, “consume you” or “destroy you.” The Hebrew word, ba‘ar, here translated “take away,” in the form here employed is used of putting away evil or the guilt of evil (Deut. 19:13, 19; etc.). The murderers’ guilt polluted the land and could be expiated only by the blood of those guilty of shedding innocent blood (Num. 35:33).

12.zh:
於是大衛吩咐少年人將他們殺了，砍斷他們的手腳，掛在希伯崙的池旁，卻將伊施波設的首級葬在希伯崙押尼珥的墳墓裡。

**掛在希伯侖的池旁。**一個公共場所，所有的人都能看見他們的屍體。砍斷手腳增加了這兩個罪犯的羞恥。將他們的屍體懸掛在公共池旁是要讓最多的人知道。這種處置對所有的人都是一個可怕的警告，說明此類罪行必得不到赦免。
**伊施波設的首級。**伊施波設個人並沒有犯什麼不名譽的罪，所以沒有理由不為他舉行體面的葬禮。
12.en:
**Over the pool.** A public place, where the bodies would be seen by all. The mutilation of the bodies added further disgrace to the criminals, and the hanging up of the corpses at the public pool gave maximum publicity to the event. Such a treatment would serve as a terrible warning to all that such crimes would not be condoned.
The head of Ish-bosheth. As an individual Ish-bosheth had shown himself guilty of no dishonor, and there was no reason why he should not be accorded an honorable burial.

1.zh:
以色列眾支派來到希伯崙見大衛，說：我們原是你的骨肉。

**眾支派。**5章至10章涉及建國和大衛早期對全國的統治。《歷代志》補充了某些有趣的細節。各支派從約旦河兩岸來到希伯侖要立大衛作王。那個場合成了歡樂的宴會。不僅長老們作為百姓的代表來了（撒下5:3），為數眾多的軍人也來參加了（代上12:23-38），還有4,600利未人，包括亞倫家的首領耶何耶大，和“少年大能的勇士”撒督（代上12:26-28）。
《撒母耳記》的事件沒有嚴格按照時間的順序排列。作者先記錄了國內的發展，再敘述國土外部的發展。
**你的骨肉。**希伯來人可能比地上所有其他民族更緊密地通過血親關係連結在一起。他們都是亞伯拉罕的子孫，與大衛本人都是骨肉（見創29:14；士9:2；撒下19:12）。這種關係也把全地的猶太人連結在一起。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–25節）**。《先祖與先知》第701-704頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–3節）**。《先祖與先知》第701頁。
1.en:
**All the tribes.** Chapters 5 to 10 deal with the establishment of the kingdom and the early part of David’s reign over the whole nation. Chronicles adds certain interesting details of the manner in which various tribes from both sides of the Jordan came to Hebron to make David king, and of the joyous festivities on that occasion. Not only did the elders come as representatives of the people (ch. 5:3) but numerous bands of armed men participated (1 Chron. 12:23–38), and 4,600 Levites, with Jehoiada as the leader of the Aaronites and Zadok as a “young man mighty of valour” (1 Chron. 12:26–28).
The events in Samuel are not arranged with a strict regard to chronology. The writer of this book describes first the internal development of the kingdom, and then the external development of the realm.
Thy bone and thy flesh. More than perhaps any other people on earth, the Hebrews were bound together by ties of kinship. They were all children of Abraham, all of the same bone and flesh as was David himself (see Gen. 29:14; Judges 9:2; 2 Sam. 19:12). The same tie still binds the Jews of all lands.

2.zh:
從前掃羅作我們王的時候，率領以色列人出入的是你；耶和華也曾應許你說：你必牧養我的民以色列，作以色列的君。

**率領以色列人出入。**見撒上18:16。百姓沒有盲目地選擇他們的領導。甚至在掃羅作王時大衛作為領袖的傑出才幹就已經顯明瞭。百姓對他的英勇和睿智有信心。
**耶和華也曾應許你說。**大衛應該作王的主要原因是耶和華已經揀選他擔任那個職位。沒有說明為什麼長老們最後提到這一點。由於對勇敢善良的耶西之子的普遍信心，由於掃羅家實際上氣數已盡，並由於上帝的旨意已經如此清楚地向著大衛，團結在大衛的領導之下顯然符合百姓的最高利益。
**你必牧養。**來自希伯來詞ra`ah（“放牧”）。這個動詞的分詞在《舊約》中譯為“牧者”（見民27:17；詩23:1等）。大衛要作全以色列的牧者。這是一個重要的人物，適合於一個通過經驗熟悉這種職務繁雜廣泛責任的人。參耶2:8；3:15等。“牧師”一詞在《新約》只出現一次（弗4:11），是從表示“牧者”的希臘詞翻譯過來的。
**君。**直譯是“統治者，”“王子。”
2.en:
**That leddest out.** See 1 Sam. 18:16. The people were not selecting their new leader blindly. Even while Saul was king the outstanding ability of David as a leader had manifested itself. The people had confidence in his prowess and sagacity.
The Lord said to thee. The main reason David should be king was that the Lord had chosen him for that position. Why the elders mentioned this point last is not revealed. With such a general confidence in the valiant and virtuous son of Jesse, with the house of Saul having practically come to an end, and with the divine will having so clearly manifested itself in behalf of David, it was obviously to the best interests of the people to unite under his leadership.
Thou shalt feed. Literally, “thou shalt pasture,” from the Heb. ra‘ah, “to pasture.” The participle of this verb is translated “shepherd” in the OT (see Num. 27:17; Ps. 23:1; etc.). David was to be a shepherd over Israel, a significant figure for one who through experience was acquainted with the multiplied and comprehensive duties of such a vocation. The word “pastor” in the KJV (Jer. 2:8; 3:15; etc.) is a translation of this same Hebrew word. The single occurrence of “pastor” in the NT (Eph. 4:11) is the translation of the Greek word for “shepherd.”
Captain. Literally, “ruler,” “prince.”

3.zh:
於是以色列的長老都來到希伯崙見大衛王，大衛在希伯崙耶和華面前與他們立約，他們就膏大衛作以色列的王。

**長老都來。**長老們作為百姓的代表和代言人。還來了還有許多戰士和祭司，都表示對耶西兒子的效忠（代上12:23-38）。成千上萬的人群集到希伯侖參加這次加冕典禮。
**立約。**約的細節雖然沒有列出來，但顯然是關於王的特權與國民權利的某些諒解，可能涉及戰爭的領導權，避免支派不公的現象，掃羅家餘剩之人的政治避難，國家軍隊的規模和徵兵的方式等問題。
**作以色列的王。**大衛先前已受膏作猶大的王（撒下2:4）。
3.en:
**All the elders.** The elders acted as the representatives and spokesmen of the people. With them came many of the warriors and the priests to acknowledge their allegiance to the son of Jesse (1 Chron. 12:23–38). Many thousands thronged to Hebron for the coronation ceremonies.
Made a league. The details of the agreement are not given, but there was evidently some understanding as to the prerogatives of the king and the rights of the subjects. There may have been reference to such matters as leadership in war, freedom from tribal partiality, political asylum for the remnant of the house of Saul, the size of the national army, and the manner of securing recruits, etc.
Over Israel. David had previously been anointed king over Judah (ch. 2:4).

4.zh:
大衛登基的時候年三十歲，在位四十年；

**三十歲。**關於與掃羅的年紀之間的關係，見本卷註釋132頁。大衛作王40年，所以他死時70歲，被形容為“年紀老邁”（代上29:28），可能是從他度了努力的一生這個角度來說的。
4.en: **Thirty years old.** For the relationship between the ages of David and Saul see p. 132. Since David reigned 40 years, he was 70 years old at his death, described as “a good old age” (1 Chron. 29:28), probably from the point of view of one who had lived a strenuous life.

6.zh:
大衛和跟隨他的人到了耶路撒冷，要攻打住那地方的耶布斯人。耶布斯人對大衛說：你若不趕出瞎子、瘸子，必不能進這地方；心裡想大衛決不能進去。

**到了耶路撒冷。**大衛被膏立為全以色列的王之後，看出需要一個比希伯侖更好的地方作他的首都。希伯侖在希伯來人所佔疆土的最南端。他顯然更喜歡他的首都仍在猶大，而耶路撒冷就是一個理想的地點（見書15:63；士1:21）。約書亞曾擊敗和殺死過耶路撒冷王（書10:23-26；12:10）。後來這座城被猶大人攻佔並燒燬了（見士1:8）。但是佔據耶路撒冷的耶布斯人並沒有被徹底征服，在被驅逐之後要麼繼續佔據著城的一部分要麼又把它奪回去了（書15:63；士1:21；19:11,12）。把耶布斯人從這個重要的據點趕走對大衛在全以色列作王的開端來說是一次重大的勝利。
**趕出瞎子。**這句話令註釋者們困惑，提出了許多解釋。其中最合理結實的可能就是耶布斯人說：“你進不了這城，只要瞎子和瘸子就能使你進不來”。即耶布斯的居民深信他們的城池堅固，並嘲笑大衛沒有能力攻取他們的堡壘，告訴他瞎子瘸子就足以把守這城，對付以色列軍隊的進攻了。
這座耶布斯人的要塞是在摩利亞山南邊的錫安山上。聖殿後來就建造在摩利亞山這塊高地上。錫安山兩邊都是深谷，是極好的防禦地形（本卷註釋625頁地圖）。
**懷愛倫註釋（6–7節）**。《先祖與先知》第703頁。
6.en:
**Went to Jerusalem.** As soon as David was anointed king over all Israel, he saw the need of a better site than Hebron for his capital. Hebron was in the extreme south of the territory occupied by the Hebrews. He evidently preferred to retain his capital in Judah, and Jerusalem offered an ideal site (see on Joshua 15:63; Judges 1:21). Joshua had slain and defeated the king of Jerusalem (Joshua 10:23–26; 12:10), and later the city had been taken and destroyed by Judah (see on Judges 1:7). But the Jebusites, who occupied Jerusalem, were not completely conquered, and either continued to hold at least a part of the city or retook it after being driven out (Joshua 15:63; Judges 1:21; 19:11, 12). The dislodging of the Jebusites from this important stronghold was an important victory for David at the beginning of his reign over all Israel.
Take away the blind. This statement has puzzled commentators, and many interpretations of the passage have been given. The one that offers perhaps the most reasonable explanation has the Jebusites saying, “You will not enter the city, but the blind and the lame will keep you out.” That is, the inhabitants of Jebus had confidence in the strength of their city, and were taunting David about his inability to take their fortress, telling him that the blind and the lame would be sufficient to hold the city against the forces of Israel.
The Jebusite stronghold was on Mt. Zion, south of Mt. Moriah, the elevation on which the Temple was later built. The mountain was flanked on two sides by deep valleys, and was admirably suited for defense (see Jerusalem in Israelite Times).

7.zh:
然而大衛攻取錫安的保障，就是大衛的城。

**攻取。**防衛者認為耶布斯是攻不下來的。它已經抵擋以色列人多年了。這座城距掃羅的首都基比亞不到6.4公里，但在掃羅作王的結束時它依保持著獨立。雖然如此，耶布斯人的這座首都卻抵擋不住大衛的勇猛和和他能幹的元帥。
7.en: **Took the strong hold.** To its defenders, Jebus seemed impregnable. It had held out against the Israelites for many years. Less than 4 mi. (6.4 km.) from Saul’s capital, Gibeah, the city still maintained its independence at the close of the reign of Saul. Nevertheless the capital of the Jebusites was not able to withstand the prowess of David and his able commander.

8.zh:
當日，大衛說：誰攻打耶布斯人，當上水溝攻打我心裡所恨惡的瘸子、瞎子。從此有俗語說：在那裡有瞎子、瘸子，他不能進屋去。

**水溝。**該詞在別處只出現在詩42:7中，譯為“瀑布”。這個名詞現在被認為是指這座古城的水井。為了從這座城門外的基訓泉引水進城，耶布斯人曾開鑿了一個約15.2米的水溝，經過岩石到了一個可以聚水的水庫。這個水庫再與一個12.2米的豎井相連，豎井連有一個通到城裡的階梯或坡道。城裡的女子可以下到這個豎井的頂部，將她們的水桶下到水塔裡取水，不必冒險出城就可以獲得用水。人若通過這條水溝上到豎井，就能進入耶布斯人的首都。
這節經文譯起來有些困難。通過與代上11:6比較，可以得知大衛似乎向屬下提了一個建議，應許說完成這一進城壯舉的人將成為“首領元帥”。據代上11:6，“洗魯雅的兒子約押先上去，就作了元帥。”這樣看來，約押成為大衛軍隊元帥，是由於他奪取了耶布斯要塞（見《先祖與先知》703頁）。
**心裡所恨惡的。**這是希伯來原文旁註的翻譯。原文是“他們恨惡大衛的心”。
**瘸子，瞎子。**在佔據進城的一個入口之後，給大衛軍隊的主力打開城門就比較容易了，因為可能只有很少的衛兵守在城牆上。耶布斯人曾奚落大衛說，瘸子和瞎子就足以把守這城使他攻不進去（見6節註釋）；因此大衛現在就用這兩個詞指守城的人。
**那裡有瞎子、瘸子。**引用的這種俗語意思不明確。“進屋”，七十士譯本為“進耶和華的屋”
8.en:
**The gutter.** The word thus translated occurs elsewhere only in Ps. 42:7, where it is rendered “waterspout.” The term is now thought to apply to the water shaft of the ancient city. To bring water into the city from the spring Gihon, which was without the city gates, the Jebusites had cut a conduit some 50 ft. (15.2 m.) through the rock to a place where the water was collected in a reservoir. This, in turn, was connected by a 40-ft. (12.2-m.) vertical shaft with the foot of a stairway or ramp that led into the city. Women in the city would descend to the top of the shaft, drop their buckets into the cistern, and thus secure water without the necessity of venturing outside the city. By making one’s way through the watercourse and up the shaft, it might be possible to enter the Jebusite capital.
The verse presents some difficulties of translation. It would seem, from a comparison with 1 Chron. 11:6, that David made a proposal to his men promising that the man who accomplished the feat of entering the city should be “chief and captain.” According to 1 Chron. 11:6, “Joab the son of Zeruiah went first up, and was chief.” It thus appears that Joab secured his position as commander of the armies of David from his successful capture of the Jebusite stronghold (see PP 703).
The lame and the blind. After an entrance into the city had been gained, it would probably be a comparatively easy task to open the gates to the main body of David’s forces, since, perhaps, only a small force of defenders would be on the city walls. The Jebusites had hurled at David the taunt that the lame and the blind would be sufficient to hold the city against him (see on v. 6); hence David now appears to use that term for the city’s defenders.
That are hated of David’s soul. This is a translation of the marginal reading of the Hebrew text. The text itself reads, “They hate the soul of David.”
The blind and the lame. The meaning of the proverbial expression thus introduced is not clear. To “house,” the LXX adds, “of the Lord.”

9.zh:
大衛住在保障裡，給保障起名叫大衛城。大衛又從米羅以裡，周圍築牆。

**米羅。**可能是耶布斯城內的某種陽臺或防禦工事，在大衛奪取耶路撒冷之前就有的，後來的列王又在其上增添了許多附屬設施（見代上11:8；王上9:15,24；11:27；王下12:20；代下32:5）。
**以裡。**米羅可能是大衛城的東北界。東邊陡峭的汲淪谷提供了堅固的天然防線。大衛所有的建築因而都在米羅以南並用米羅來保護北部。加強該城防禦的任務交給了約押（代上11:8）。
9.en:
**Millo.** Probably some kind of terrace or fortification in the Jebusite city, already there when David captured Jerusalem, and to which numerous additions were made by later kings (see 1 Chron. 11:8; 1 Kings 9:15, 24; 11:27; 2 Kings 12:20; 2 Chron. 32:5).
And inward. Millo may have been the northeastern limit of the City of David. To the east the precipitous ravine of Kidron provided a strong natural defense. All David’s buildings would then be to the south of Millo and protected by it on the north. The work of further strengthening the city’s defenses was committed to Joab (1 Chron. 11:8).

10.zh:
大衛日見強盛，因為耶和華─萬軍之神與他同在。

**與他同在。**參代上11:9。大衛的成功不僅是由於他個人的努力和英勇，而且是因為上帝的臨格與祝福。人一生中最終的成功不是靠人力也不是靠智慧取得的，而是靠耶和華的靈取得的（見亞4:6）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第702頁。
10.en: **With him.** Compare 1 Chron. 11:9. The success of David was due not only to his own effort and prowess but to the presence and blessing of God. Ultimate success in life comes not by human might nor wisdom but by the Spirit of the Lord (see Zech. 4:6).

11.zh:
推羅王希蘭將香柏木運到大衛那裡，又差遣使者和木匠、石匠給大衛建造宮殿。

**希蘭。**有人問這個希蘭是不是幫助所羅門建造聖殿的那個希蘭（王上5:1；代下2:3）。若是這兩個希蘭是同一個人，那他作王的時間就異常長久。當然這不是不可能的。本章的事件發生在大衛作王的初期，而與所羅門有聯繫的希蘭在所羅門作王第24年時還在（王上9:10-14；參王上6:1,38；7:1）。如果這兩個希蘭是同一個人的話，那麼他作王就超過50年了。反對這種把兩個王看成是一個人的觀點是由約瑟弗斯提出的，因為幫助所羅門的希蘭作王為期34年（Against Apion 1. 18）。但約瑟弗斯年代記錄的準確性不一定可靠。
**差遣使者。**希蘭尋求結盟。這是對大衛權勢的敬意。
**給大衛建造宮殿。**腓尼基人（見67-69頁）當時在建造的經驗和技巧方面遠遠超過希伯來人，因為大衛和所羅門都主要倚賴他們建造自己的宮殿和聖殿。考古學家證實在巴勒斯坦，希伯來人早期的石工工程不如他們之前的迦南人。腓尼基人就屬於迦南人。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–18節）**。《先祖與先知》第703頁。
11.en:
**Hiram.** There is some question as to whether this Hiram is the same as the Hiram who assisted Solomon in the building of the Temple (1 Kings 5:1; 2 Chron. 2:3). Considering the two to be identical appears to assign an unusually long, though not impossible, reign to one king. The events of this chapter took place early in David’s reign, whereas the Hiram connected with Solomon was still alive in the 24th year of Solomon’s reign (1 Kings 9:10–14; cf. 6:1, 38; 7:1); this would make a total of more than 50 years of reign if the two Hirams were the same. Against the view claiming the two kings to be identical is the statement by Josephus that the Hiram who assisted Solomon ruled for 34 years (Against Apion 1. 18). However, Josephus’ chronological statements cannot always be trusted for accuracy.
Sent messengers. Hiram sought the alliance. This was a tribute to David’s power.
Built David an house. The Phoenicians (see pp. 67–69) at this time had much more experience and skill in building than had the Hebrews, for both David and Solomon relied heavily upon them in the construction both of their palaces and the Temple. Archeologists confirm that the masonry of the early Hebrew period in Palestine was inferior to that of the Canaanites, who preceded them, and to whom the Phoenicians belonged.

12.zh:
大衛就知道耶和華堅立他作以色列王，又為自己的民以色列使他的國興旺。

**為自己的民以色列。**耶和華因大衛的信實和忠誠祝福了他。祂也因自己要使希伯來民族成為地上的屬靈國度而祝福大衛。大衛在接管了選民積極進取的領導權之後遵行了上天的旨意。這樣的做法總是能帶來成功與祝福。
12.en: **His people Israel’s sake.** The Lord blessed David because of his own faithfulness and fidelity. He also blessed him because of His purpose to make the Hebrew people a spiritual kingdom upon earth. In taking over the aggressive leadership of the chosen people, David was working in harmony with the purposes of Heaven. Such a program always brings success and blessing.

13.zh:
大衛離開希伯崙之後，在耶路撒冷又立后妃，又生兒女。

**又立后妃。**在實力增加並日益興旺的同時，以色列越來越隨從周圍國家做法的試探與危險也臨到了。擁有龐大的後宮是東方君主的習俗，大衛隨從了這一風俗。在這件事上大衛做錯了，因為上帝曾吩咐：“他也不可為自己多立妃嬪，恐怕他的心偏邪”（申17:17）。大衛的繼任者效法了他的榜樣，給自己帶來了危害。
**兒女。**大衛在希伯侖和耶路撒冷所生的兒子共有19個（見代上3:1-9）。除了他瑪以外（代上3:9），女兒的名字沒有列出。
13.en:
**More concubines and wives.** With the increasing strength and prosperity came temptation and the danger that Israel would follow more and more in the ways of the nations about. It was the custom of Eastern monarchs to have a large harem, and David followed this custom. In this David did wrong, for the Lord had commanded: “Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away” (Deut. 17:17). The example set by David was followed by his successors, to their harm.
Sons and daughters. The total number of sons born to David, in Hebron and in Jerusalem, was 19 (see 1 Chron. 3:1–9). The names of the daughters, except Tamar (1 Chron. 3:9), are not given.

14.zh:
在耶路撒冷所生的兒子是沙母亞、朔罷、拿單、所羅門、

這裡提到的兒子（14-16節）是在耶路撒冷出生的；關於在希伯侖出生的兒子，見撒下3:2-5。這份名單在代上3:5-8；14:4-7中稍有差異。在耶路撒冷生的頭四個兒子是拔示巴所生的（代上3:5）。因而他們是在大衛作王的稍後時期出生的。所有的名單都把所羅門列在拔示巴生的四個兒子最後，但是撒下12:24卻表明他是存活的子女中壽命年長的（見撒下12:14）。名單中的差異不一定是抄寫的錯誤。本節沒有提到的兩個名字在《歷代志》的名單卻有；基利押（撒下3:3）則被稱為但以利。首先是記錄不完整的問題，其次可能只是一個兒子不只有一個名字。
14.en: **The names.** The sons here mentioned (vs. 14–16) were born in Jerusalem; for those born in Hebron see ch. 3:2–5. The same list, with some variations, is found in 1 Chron. 3:5–8; 14:4–7. The first four born in Jerusalem were the children of Bathsheba (1 Chron. 3:5). They were consequently born at a later period of David’s reign. All lists place Solomon last among the four sons of Bathsheba, but 2 Sam. 12:24 would indicate that he was the eldest of the surviving children (see 2 Sam. 12:14). The variations in these lists do not necessarily mean scribal errors. Two names not mentioned in this passage are found in the Chronicles list, and Chileab (2 Sam. 3:3) is called Daniel. The first is a matter of incompleteness, the second may merely indicate that one son bore more than one name.

17.zh:
非利士人聽見人膏大衛作以色列王，非利士眾人就上來尋索大衛；大衛聽見，就下到保障。

**非利士人聽見。**大衛在作王的初期並沒有與非利士人作對。他被掃羅驅趕時曾受到非利士人的善待。大衛成為猶大王后，他們還希望與他聯合對付掃羅的家。他們確信自己對分裂的希伯來國持有優勢。但當大衛成為全以色列的王，成功地奪取了耶布斯，並與推羅的希蘭結盟後，非利士人就擔心大衛的實力增長，決定要與以色列作戰，抑制這位新王的勢力。
**保障。**mesudah，“要塞，堡壘。”該詞還用在第7節中，顯然指同一個堡壘（見《先祖與先知》703，704頁）。
17.en:
**When the Philistines heard.** During the early years of his reign David had had no difficulty with the Philistines. In the time of his exile from Saul the Philistines had befriended him, and when David became king of Judah they hoped for friendship from him in opposition to Saul’s house. They felt confident that they could retain their power over a divided Hebrew nation. But when David became king over all Israel, and succeeded in capturing Jebus and effected an alliance with Hiram of Tyre, the Philistines, fearing David’s growing strength, determined to make war against Israel and curb the power of its new king.
Hold. Heb. meṣudah, “the stronghold.” The same Hebrew word is used in v. 7, and evidently the same fortification is meant (see PP 703, 704).

18.zh:
非利士人來了，佈散在利乏音谷。

**利乏音谷。**在書15:8中譯為“欣嫩子谷”。這是一個多產的山谷，延伸到耶路撒冷西南，提供了充足的空間可以紮營。
**懷愛倫註釋（18–25節）**。《先祖與先知》第704頁。
18.en: **The valley of Rephaim.** The phrase is translated “the valley of the giants” in Joshua 15:8. It was a fruitful valley extending to the southwest of Jerusalem, and provided ample room for a large encampment.

19.zh:
大衛求問耶和華說：我可以上去攻打非利士人嗎？你將他們交在我手裡嗎？耶和華說：你可以上去，我必將非利士人交在你手裡。

**求問耶和華。**見撒下2:1註釋。
我可以上去攻打非利士人嗎？不是字面意義上的“上去”，因為非利士人在山谷裡（見士1:1；12:3；撒上7:7）。
**必交在。**這個動詞是強調的。
19.en:
**Enquired of the Lord.** See on ch. 2:1.
Shall I go up? That is, to battle, not literally, “up,” for the Philistines were in a valley (see Judges 1:1; 12:3; 1 Sam. 7:7).
Doubtless deliver. Rather, “surely deliver.” The Hebrew has no adverb, but the construction is such as to require an emphatic translation of the verb.

20.zh:
大衛來到巴力毘拉心，在那裡擊殺非利士人，說：耶和華在我面前沖破敵人，如同水沖去一般。因此稱那地方為巴力毘拉心。

**巴力毗拉心。**直譯是“突破之主”或“爆破的所有者。”大衛突襲非利士人，衝破了他們的防線，席捲了他面前的一切。在耶和華的幫助下，以色列軍隊摧毀了敵軍的抵抗，就像大水衝破了水壩一樣。他們獲得這次勝利之後，這個地方可能就定名為巴力毗拉心。
20.en: **Baal-perazim.** Literally, “lord of the breaking through” or “possessor of the burstings.” Making a sudden attack upon the Philistines, David broke through their ranks and carried all before him. With the help of the Lord, the forces of Israel burst through the enemy resistance as waters burst through a dam. It was probably after their victory here that they named the place Baal-perazim.

21.zh:
非利士人將偶像撇在那裡，大衛和跟隨他的人拿去了。

**偶像。**來自希伯來詞`asab。代上14:12中相似的詞是'elohim（“神像”）。非利士人冒險參戰時，隨軍帶著他們眾神的神像，指望可以保證獲勝。他奔逃時把神像丟下，表明他們是突然潰退的。
**拿去了。**根據代上14:12，應理解為“焚燒了”。
21.en:
**Images.** From the Heb. ‘aṣab, everywhere else translated “idol.” The parallel reference in 1 Chron. 14:12 has ’elohim, “gods.” When the Philistines ventured into battle they took the images of their gods with them, expecting thus to assure victory. The suddenness of the rout is indicated by the fact that in their flight they left their gods behind them.
Burned them. Literally, “took them away.” That the phrase should be understood as the KJV has translated it, is evident from 1 Chron. 14:12.

22.zh:
非利士人又上來，佈散在利乏音谷。

**又上來。**這次的敗北激發了非利士人更大的努力。他們聚集了更大的軍隊，又來與大衛作對，決心要獲得勝利。
22.en: **Yet again.** The defeat only stirred the Philistines to greater efforts. Gathering still larger forces, they again came against David, determined to gain the victory.

23.zh:
大衛求問耶和華；耶和華說：不要一直地上去，要轉到他們後頭，從桑林對面攻打他們。

**求問耶和華。**見19節。大衛先前的勝利並沒有使他驕傲自負。他現在習慣尋求上帝的指導。
**不要一直地上去。**見19節，耶和華指示大衛要“上去”。敵軍已經回到了原來的戰場，並顯然預料大衛會使用與先前一樣的戰術。這次他們無疑為直接攻擊作好了準備。但是耶和華指示大衛不要正面進攻。
**轉到後頭。**大衛迂迴到敵軍後面，從意外的方向發動進攻，獲得了勝利。上帝運用不同的方法把勝利賜給祂的子民。有時尋求上帝幫助的人奉命只要靜靜站著觀看耶和華的拯救（見出14:13,14；王下19:7,32,35）。在其它時候，救助來自上帝指導和祝福人的努力。人在向上帝提出請求後，儘自己的力量成就它，並不能證明這個人缺乏信心。
**桑林。**不能確定是什麼植物。有是版本為“香脂樹”。
23.en:
**Enquired of the Lord.** See v. 19. David’s previous victory did not make him self-confident or conceited. To ask guidance from God was now his custom.
Not go up. See v. 19, where David was instructed by the Lord to “go up.” The enemy had returned to the same battleground and evidently expected David to employ the same method of attack as previously. This time they doubtless prepared for such a direct assault. But the Lord instructed David not to make a frontal attack.
Fetch a compass. That is, “Go around to their rear” (RSV). By making a circuit around the enemy and attacking them from an unexpected quarter, David gained the victory. God operates in various ways to give victory to His people. Sometimes those who have asked for divine aid are instructed simply to stand still and see the salvation of the Lord (see Ex. 14:13, 14; 2 Kings 19:7, 32, 35). At other times deliverance comes through God’s directing and blessing human effort. There is no manifestation of a lack of faith in one who, after presenting a petition to God, does all in his power to bring about its fulfillment.
Mulberry trees. The botanical identification is uncertain. Some versions read “balsam” (see RSV).

24.zh:
你聽見桑樹梢上有腳步的聲音，就要急速前去，因為那時耶和華已經在你前頭去攻打非利士人的軍隊。

**腳步。**se`adah，直譯是“行軍。”這聲音對大衛來說是上帝的信號。上帝會與他同在，天軍會行在他前面。se`ad的陽性形式用在士5:4和詩68:7中，指萬軍之耶和華行走。
**急速前去。**在耶和華的工作中，有我們必須做的部分。那些懶惰地袖手旁觀，指望耶和華行事，自己卻什麼都不做的人，除非耶和華有這樣的指示，否則必定失敗。上帝吩咐大衛和他的百姓急速前去，並應許說那時祂就會在他們前面擊打非利士軍隊。上帝的應許那時和現在都是有條件的。當我們盡到自己的職責時，上帝必盡祂的職責。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷五第728頁。
24.en:
**Going.** Heb. ṣe‘adah, literally, “marching.” The sound was to be to him a divine signal that God would be with him and that the armies of heaven would march before him. The masculine form ṣe‘ad is employed in Judges 5:4 and Ps. 68:7 of the march of the hosts of God.
Bestir thyself. In the work of the Lord we must do our part. Those who sit idly by, expecting the Lord to act while they do nothing, unless the Lord has so directed, must expect defeat. God gave the word that David and his people were to bestir themselves, and promised that then He would go before them to smite the hosts of the Philistines. God’s promises, then and now, are conditional. When we do our part God will do His.

25.zh:
大衛就遵著耶和華所吩咐的去行，攻打非利士人，從迦巴直到基色。

**大衛就遵著耶和華所吩咐的去行。**大衛成功的秘訣很簡單；他精確地照上帝指示去做。當人將自己的意願置於上帝的旨意之上時，就必招致失敗。我們不一定能明白上帝發命令的原因，這也並不總是必要的。所要求於我們的就是信任和順從。大衛絕對服從上帝的指示，結果獲得又一場偉大勝利。
**從迦巴。**七十士譯本為“基遍”，與代上14:16的相應段落一樣。迦巴是現在的Jeba`，在耶路撒冷東北差不多9.6公里處，而基遍位於耶路撒冷西北同樣距離處，在從利乏音谷到基色撤退的道路上。
**基色。**是一個俯瞰亞雅侖谷的堡壘，在基遍以西24公里處，現名Tell Jezer，已經發掘出來，出土了豐富的考古學證據。當耶路撒冷王、希伯侖王、耶末王、拉吉王和伊磯倫王攻打基遍時，約書亞追擊他們到伯和侖的山口並在亞雅侖谷獲得了一場著名的勝利，日頭在那裡停住了（書10:1-14）。這無疑是大衛現在擊潰非利士人的相同路線，因為從基遍到基色的路經過亞雅侖谷。朝耶路撒冷西北方向逃跑，是因為大衛轉到非利士人後頭，從南部攻擊他們，把他們往北趕往基遍，再逃往基色。在《歷代志上》的相應記載中，這些戰役發生在大衛不成功地（代上13:5-14）和成功地（代上15）將約櫃運回耶路撒冷的兩次努力之間（代上14:8-17）。《歷代志上》還記錄其間希蘭幫助大衛建造宮殿，大衛在耶路撒冷生的孩子（代上14:1-7）。值得注意的是《撒母耳記下》和《歷代志上》所記錄事件的順序不一定相同。有時不能確定所涉及的時間的細節。顯然事件順序的重要性比不上其中的屬靈教訓。見《先祖與先知》703，704頁，那裡並沒有遵循《撒母耳記下》的順序。
25.en:
**David did so.** The secret of David’s success was simple; he did precisely what God instructed him to do. When man puts his will above God’s will he invites defeat. We will not always understand the reasons for God’s commands, nor is this always necessary. All we are expected to do is to trust and obey. David implicitly obeyed the divine directions, and as a result there followed another great victory.
From Geba. The LXX reads, Gibeon. This is also the reading of the parallel passage in 1 Chron. 14:16. Geba, modern Jeba‘, is nearly 6 mi. (9.6 km.) northeast of Jerusalem and Gibeon, ej–Jib, the same distance to the northwest. Evidently Gibeon is meant, for it lay directly in the path of retreat from the Valley of Rephaim to Gezer.
Gazer. Or Gezer. A fortress overlooking the Valley of Aijalon, 15 mi. west of Gibeon. The site, now called Tell Jezer, has been excavated and has yielded rich archeological evidence. When the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon attacked Gibeon, Joshua pursued them down the pass of Beth-horon and gained a notable victory over them in the Valley of Aijalon, where the sun was caused to stand still (Joshua 10:1–14). This was doubtless the same route now covered by David in his rout of the Philistines, for the road from Gibeon to Gezer led through the Valley of Aijalon. The flight in this northwesterly direction from Jerusalem was determined by the fact that David had “fetched a compass” around the Philistines, attacking them from the south and thus driving them to the north to Gibeon and thence toward Gezer. In the parallel account these battles are placed between David’s unsuccessful (1 Chron. 13:5–14) and his successful (1 Chron. 15) attempt to bring the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chron. 14:8–17). But Chronicles also records Hiram’s assistance to David in the building of his house and the record of the children born to him at Jerusalem (1 Chron. 14:1–7) between his unsuccessful and successful efforts to bring the ark there. It will thus be noted that the sequence of events as recorded in 2 Sam. and 1 Chron. is not always the same. It is sometimes impossible to determine the exact details of the chronology involved. Evidently the order of events is less important than the facts themselves and the spiritual lessons to be gained from them. See PP 703, 704, which follows the sequence of 2 Sam.

1.zh:
王住在自己宮中，耶和華使他安靖，不被四圍的仇敵擾亂。

**王住在自己宮中。**“住”或譯成“坐”（見2節）。王宮建成之後。大衛開始想到自己住在美好的宮中，卻沒有一個地方可以被稱為上帝的殿，這是多麼不相宜。見代上17章中的相似記載。
**安靖。**這段和平的時期使大衛有時間和精力去做別的事情。在這種情況下，他開始打算建一座敬拜上帝的殿。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–29節）**。《先祖與先知》第711-713頁。
1.en:
**Sat in his house.** The word here translated “sat” also means “to dwell” and is frequently so rendered (see v. 2). The context seems to demand such a rendering here. The idea is, “while the king dwelt in his own house,” that is, after it had been built. David began to think of the inconsistency of having a beautiful home of his own but no place that could be called the house of God. See the parallel account of the events of this chapter in 1 Chron. 17.
Rest round about. The period of peace permitted David to give his time and energy to other things. Under these circumstances he began to contemplate the building of a temple for the worship of God.

2.zh:
那時，王對先知拿單說：看哪，我住在香柏木的宮中，神的約櫃反在幔子裡。

**對先知拿單說。**這是第一次提到先知拿單，但是他顯然已經是王信任的顧問了，大衛與他商討重要的事情，想得到來自上帝的明確指示。在大衛作王和所羅門作王時期，拿單都是一個重要人物（見撒下12；王上1:10-12,34,38）。
**幔子。**參出26和36章。安放約櫃的帳幕是一個臨時性建築，可能與摩西的帳幕相似。原來的帳幕和燔祭壇都在基遍（代上21:29；代下1:3-6）。連同耶路撒冷帳幕裡的約櫃，就有兩個全國性的敬拜場所了。但耶和華的旨意是隻應有一個敬拜中心（申12:13,14），大衛計劃在耶路撒冷建一個全國性的大聖殿。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–3節）**。《先祖與先知》第750頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–10節）**。《先祖與先知》第711頁。
2.en:
**Unto Nathan.** This is the first mention of Nathan the prophet, but he was evidently already a confidential counselor of the king, to be consulted on important matters in which David desired specific directions from God. Nathan became a prominent figure in David’s reign and also in the reign of Solomon (see 2 Sam. 12; 1 Kings 1:10–12, 34, 38).
Within curtains. The word for “curtains” is that used in Ex. 26 and 36 for the covering of the tabernacle. The tent in which the ark was housed was a temporary structure probably similar to the Mosaic tabernacle. The original tabernacle and the altar of burnt offering were at Gibeon (1 Chron. 21:29; 2 Chron. 1:3–6). With the ark in a tent in Jerusalem, there were now two national shrines. It was the Lord’s purpose, however, that there should be only one central place of worship (Deut. 12:13, 14), and it was David’s plan to establish one great national shrine in Jerusalem.

3.zh:
拿單對王說：你可以照你的心意而行，因為耶和華與你同在。

**拿單說。**拿單是一位先知，但是此刻顯然表達的是他私人的意見。先知只有在上帝賜給他靈感信息的時候才能給人以這樣的信息。先知的特權是面對難題時祈求靈感的答案，但是給不給答案卻出於耶和華。有時耶和華認為讓人們做他們自己的決定，從而發展明智判斷的才能更好。在其它時候祂樂於給出一道神聖的信息。這種上帝的啟示通常以獨特的句子引出：“耶和華如此說”（見5節）。
**照你的心意而行。**大衛表達的願望似乎是良好的，拿單自然認為王實行這個計劃是正當的。然而先知卻還沒有接到任何批准的信息。他是照著自己感覺說的，而不是照著上帝的啟示回答的。
3.en:
**Nathan said.** Nathan was a prophet, but at the moment was evidently expressing his own private opinion. A prophet can give to men an inspired message only if God has given to him such a message. It is the prophet’s privilege when confronted with a difficult question to pray for an inspired answer, but the disposition of the answer is of the Lord. There are times when the Lord sees it is better for men to make their own decisions and thus develop the faculty of wise judgment. At other times He is pleased to send a divine message. Such divine communications are frequently qualified by the distinguishing statement, “Thus saith the Lord” (see v. 5).
Go, do all. The purpose expressed by David appeared good and Nathan naturally thought that it was right for the king to carry it into execution. The prophet, however, had not received any confirmatory message. He spoke according to his own sense of right, and not in response to divine revelation.

4.zh:
當夜，耶和華的話臨到拿單說：

**耶和華的話臨到。**這是上帝信息的明確標誌（見第3節註釋），與拿單早先的意見截然相反。然而當拿單受命回到王那裡承認自己先前的錯誤時，並沒有表現出絲毫的不滿。一個人承認錯誤並優雅地改正錯誤需要有上帝的恩典。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–13節）**。《服務真詮》第473頁。
4.en: **Word of the Lord came.** The communication was distinctly marked as coming from God (see on v. 3), and was in direct opposition to Nathan’s earlier expressed view. There is no evidence, however, of any spirit of rebellion on the part of Nathan when he was asked to return to the king and acknowledge his previous error. It requires divine grace to admit that one has made a mistake and to set about graciously to rectify the error.

5.zh:
你去告訴我僕人大衛，說耶和華如此說：你豈可建造殿宇給我居住呢？

**我僕人大衛。**大衛是上帝的僕人。他本人曾受聖靈感動說話，比如他在寫作《詩篇》時那樣。他也被稱為“先知”（徒2:30）。在次耶和華選擇不直接對他說話，而是通過另一位先知告訴他。上帝通過不同的人作工，並且神聖的亮光通過不同的渠道臨到。今天也是這樣，上帝通過祂的教會組織作工並呼召弟兄們之間互愛與信任，警告個人獨立的危險。如果大衛有驕傲的觀念，那麼當他的想法被取消時，就會大大激怒。但他接受了上帝的責備，雖然這與他本人的意圖和先知的判斷相反。
**耶和華如此說。**當帶有這個標誌的信息臨到時，人就應當聽從。如果懷疑信息的真實性（見約壹4:1），聖經已告訴我們如何試驗信息的有效性（民12:6；申13:1-3；18:22；太7:15-20；約壹4:1-3）。我們有責任瞭解信息的來源。如果是出於上帝的，就要遵行。
豈可建造殿宇給我居住呢？這個問題暗示否定的回答。代上17:4相應的句子是“你不可建造殿宇給我居住”（代上17:4）。
5.en:
**My servant David.** David was a servant of God and had himself spoken by inspiration, as in the composition of his psalms. To him also applied the title “prophet” (Acts 2:30). On this occasion the Lord chose to speak to him not directly, but through another prophet. God works through different individuals and divine light comes through various channels.
