The system of forced labor came to be such a thorn in the flesh of the Israelites during Solomon’s reign that Adoram was stoned to death during the early difficulties of Rehoboam’s reign when the northern tribes revolted (1 Kings 12:18).
Jehoshaphat. Mentioned in the early list of David’s officers. He still held the same office during the reign of Solomon (1 Kings 4:3). For his work, see on 2 Sam. 8:16.

25.zh:
示法作書記；撒督和亞比亞他作祭司長；

**撒督和亞比亞他。**以前曾提到撒督和“亞比亞他的兒子亞希米勒”為祭司（撒下8:17）。但這份名單屬於大衛作王的後期。所以看到兒子似乎在父親之前作祭司，很令人驚訝。關於這些人，見撒下8:17註釋。
25.en: **Zadok and Abiathar.** Earlier Zadok and “Ahimelech the son of Abiathar” were named as the priests (ch. 8:17). The present list, however, is for a later period of David’s reign, and it is surprising, therefore, to see that the son seems to have preceded his father as priest. For a discussion of these men see on ch. 8:17.

26.zh:
睚珥人以拉作大衛的宰相。

**睚珥人的以拉。**這位官員沒有列在撒下8:16-18的名單中，也沒有列在代上18:14-17的名單中。據推測他與撒下23:38大衛勇士中的“以帖人以拉”可能是同一個人，但關於這一點聖經沒有說明。
26.en: **Ira also the Jairite.** This officer is not listed in ch. 8:16–18 nor in 1 Chron. 18:14–17. It has been conjectured that “Ira an Ithrite,” listed among David’s mighty men in 2 Sam. 23:38, may be the same man, but the Word is silent on this point.

1.zh:
大衛年間有饑荒，一連三年，大衛就求問耶和華。耶和華說：這饑荒是因掃羅和他流人血之家殺死基遍人。

**大衛年間有饑荒。**這裡的用詞比較含糊，不能確定這場饑荒是否緊接著撒下20章的事件。沒有關於這場饑荒發生時間的證據。也沒有理由懷疑它是在大衛作王臨近結束時困擾他的麻煩之一。但它也可能發生在大衛恩待約拿單的兒子米非波設之後的任何時間（7節）。大衛作王期間的事件不一定嚴格按時間順序記錄。
**求問耶和華。**大衛推斷這場饑荒必有原因。耶和華曾告訴祂的子民，要是他們不順從，祂就會扣留祂的福氣（申28:15,23,24），所以大衛為眼下這場饑荒的原因求問上帝。
**掃羅……殺死基遍人。**這是掃羅傷害基遍人的唯一記錄。在以色列人征服迦南的時候，基遍人曾通過詭計與約書亞立約。根據這約的條款，他們可以在服苦役的狀況下存活（書9:3-27）。
1.en:
**Then there was a famine.** Literally, “And there was a famine.”
In the days of David. This phrase is too vague to warrant the conclusion that this famine must have followed immediately the events of ch. 20. There is no evidence as to exactly when this famine took place. There is no reason to doubt that it was one of the troubles that beset David toward the close of his reign, although it could have happened at any time after David’s kindness to Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth (v. 7). Not all the events in David’s reign are recorded in strict chronological sequence.
Enquired of the Lord. David concluded that there must be some reason for the famine. The Lord had told His people that if they were disobedient He would withhold His blessings (Deut. 28:15, 23, 24), and David now sought the Lord for the reason for this present famine.
He slew the Gibeonites. This is the only record of Saul’s offense against the Gibeonites. At the time of the conquest of Canaan the Gibeonites had succeeded through guile in making a league with Joshua. According to the terms of this league they were to be allowed to live with Israel in a state of servitude (Joshua 9:3–27).

2.zh:
原來這基遍人不是以色列人，乃是亞摩利人中所剩的；以色列人曾向他們起誓，不殺滅他們，掃羅卻為以色列人和猶大人發熱心，想要殺滅他們。大衛王召了他們來，

**亞摩利人。**據書9:7；11:19，基遍人是希未人。在列舉巴勒斯坦的許多土著民族時，希未人與亞摩利人是分別列出的（創10:16,17；書9:1；11:3；12:8）。但是“亞摩利人”常常泛指“迦南人”，即迦南的任何居民（創15:16；申1:27）。“亞摩利人”有時也特指巴勒斯坦丘陵地區的居民，以別於平原地區的迦南人（民13:29；申1:7,20）。因此希未人包括在“亞摩利人”的後一種意義中，指住在山地的迦南人。
**曾向他們起誓。**見書9:15,19-21。約書亞和會眾的首領與基遍人立了一個莊嚴的誓約，承諾必不殺他們，而是允許他們住在這地上。以色列的首領們認為自己應該受這個莊嚴誓約的約束。他們也認識到要是他們違背了這誓約，就必有嚴重的後果。
**為以色列人。**這次不是掃羅一個人違法。作為以色列的王，他是代表百姓併為百姓的利益行事的。百姓無疑是贊成他去滅絕基遍人的行動，因而他們與王同樣有罪。這就可以解釋為什麼耶和華允許對掃羅所犯罪過的刑罰臨到大衛和他的百姓身上。全國都違反了約書亞和會眾首領們在400多年前所立的莊嚴誓約。在掃羅民族主義熱心的掩蓋之下，存在著自私、驕傲和自大的精神，迥異於上帝要求祂的子民所具有的謙卑、無私和高尚的宗旨。
2.en:
**The Amorites.** According to Joshua 9:7; 11:19 the people of Gibeon were Hivites, who in many enumerations of the native inhabitants of Palestine are listed separately from the Amorites (Gen. 10:16, 17; Joshua 9:1; 11:3; 12:8). But the term “Amorite” is often employed in a more comprehensive sense, somewhat equivalent to “Canaanite,” as meaning any of the inhabitants of Canaan (Gen. 15:16; Deut. 1:27). “Amorites” sometimes denotes more particularly the inhabitants of the hill country of Palestine as distinct from the Canaanites of the plain (Num. 13:29; Deut. 1:7, 20). The Hivites would thus be included in this latter usage of “Amorites” to mean hill dwellers of Canaan.
Had sworn unto them. See Joshua 9:15, 19–21. Joshua, together with the princes of the congregation, had made a solemn oath that the Gibeonites would not be slain but that they would be permitted to abide in the land. The leaders of Israel regarded themselves as bound by this solemn oath, and accordingly they would realize that serious consequences must inevitably follow if they violated the oath.
To the children of Israel. Or, “for the children of Israel.” In this offense Saul was not alone. As the king of Israel he was acting with the people and in their behalf. The people were doubtless in sympathy with him in his campaign to exterminate the Gibeonites, and thus the guilt rested upon them as well as upon the king. This would explain why the Lord allowed the punishment for Saul’s offense to fall upon David and his people. The whole nation was involved in the violation of the solemn oath given by Joshua and the princes of the congregation more than 400 years before. Under the cloak of Saul’s nationalistic zeal existed a spirit of selfishness, pride, and arrogance that was utterly foreign to the humility, disinterestedness, and loftiness of purpose that God required of His children.

3.zh:
問他們說：我當為你們怎樣行呢？可用什麼贖這罪，使你們為耶和華的產業祝福呢？

可用什麼贖這罪？大衛原應將這個問題向上帝提出，正如他先前就這場饑荒的起因求問上帝那樣。聖經沒有記錄大衛把這個問題帶到耶和華面前，也沒有確認基遍人所要求的事和大衛作為回應所實行的事，與上帝為糾正這種情況會提出的要求一致。
掃羅的罪是嚴重歪曲耶和華的宗教。他的態度可能反映了以色列人的普遍態度。他們甚至在掃羅死後，還繼續對住在他們中間、他們曾宣誓保護的這些異族人表示敵意。上帝的宗教必須得到維護。沒有透露為達到這個目的上帝有什麼要求。
向受害人承認錯誤的主要目的之一，就是盡最大的可能消除罪行的不良影響。人們已徹底灰心了。他們的生命因他們同胞的錯誤而喪失了。竭力消除罪行的起因，是成為絆腳石之人的責任。
**為耶和華的產業祝福。**除非對基遍人所犯的罪行消除了，否則以色列人就不能享有耶和華的祝福。因此要是彌補了對基遍人的錯行，他們就成了以色列民重新受祝福的手段。
3.en:
Wherewith shall I make the atonement? David should have addressed this question to God, even as he had addressed the previous inquiry concerning the cause of the famine. The record does not state that David took this matter to the Lord, nor does it affirm that what the Gibeonites demanded and what David carried out in response was in harmony with what God would have required in order to rectify the situation.
Saul’s offense had been a gross misrepresentation of the religion of Jehovah. His attitude probably reflected that of the Israelites at large, who, even after Saul’s death, continued to show hostility to these foreigners in their midst whom they had pledged to protect. It was highly essential that the religion of God be vindicated. Precisely what God would have demanded by way of achieving this end is not revealed.
One of the chief objects of confessing faults to the ones harmed is to nullify to the greatest possible extent the evil influence of the misdeed. Men have become completely discouraged and their souls have been lost as a result of the errors of their fellow men. It is the duty of the one who has been the stumbling block to try to remove the cause of offense to the best of his ability.
Bless the inheritance. Unless the offense against the Gibeonites were removed, Israel could not hope to enjoy the blessing of the Lord. Hence if the wrong against the Gibeonites were atoned for, these people would prove to be the means of bringing back blessings to the nation of Israel.

4.zh:
基遍人回答說：我們和掃羅與他家的事並不關乎金銀，也不要因我們的緣故殺一個以色列人。大衛說：你們怎樣說，我就為你們怎樣行。

**並不關乎金銀。**擊殺基遍人時可能沒收了他們的財產。真心賠償就必須歸還從他們的財物。但基遍人卻堅持說他們並不關心屬世的財物。他們願意放棄物質的賠償。
**殺一個以色列人。**以色列民族對基遍人在掃羅手下被殺負有責任。但現在不要求全體百姓支付血債。基遍人認為這罪主要應由掃羅家負責，應該由他家來補償。
4.en:
**No silver nor gold of Saul.** The smiting of the Gibeonites probably involved the confiscation of their property. It was only right that in a sincere effort to make restitution, what had been taken from them should be returned. The Gibeonites insisted, however, that they were not concerned with worldly goods. They were willing to forgo the matter of restitution in kind.
Kill any man in Israel. Israel as a nation was responsible for the slaughter of the Gibeonites at the hand of Saul. But the people as a whole would not now be asked to pay the price of the blood that had been shed. The Gibeonites were of the opinion that the guilt should rest primarily upon the house of Saul and that by it expiation should be made.

5.zh:
他們對王說：那從前謀害我們、要滅我們、使我們不得再住以色列境內的人，

**滅我們。**掃羅一定曾給基遍人帶來一場浩劫。這個民族可能被滅絕了，只剩下少數人，可能分散在全地各處。既然這一罪行主要是掃羅造成的，基遍人現在就要求由掃羅的家承擔責任。
5.en: **Consumed us.** Saul must have wrought widespread havoc among the Gibeonites. As a people they were probably all but destroyed, with only a remnant remaining, probably scattered here and there throughout the land. Since Saul was primarily responsible for this crime, the Gibeonites now asked that his house should carry the blame.

6.zh:
現在願將他的子孫七人交給我們，我們好在耶和華面前，將他們懸掛在耶和華揀選掃羅的基比亞。王說：我必交給你們。

**將他們懸掛。**基遍人可能還記得記載民25:4的事件。在巴力毗珥犯罪的民中的族長被“懸掛在耶和華面前”，以便“耶和華向以色列所發的怒氣可以消了。”然而目前的情形是不同的，因為不是犯罪者本人受到刑罰，反而是他們的子孫代為受過。
**基比亞。**七十士譯本為“基遍”，有人認為是對的（見修訂標準本）。但有充分的理由採納希伯來原文。基比亞是掃羅的家鄉（撒上10:26；11:4）。在掃羅祖籍的家補贖他的罪行似乎是合適的。那時國家的聖所確實在基遍。帳幕還在那兒。那是以色列人的獻祭之地（王上3:4；代上16:39,40；代下1:3）。但沒有理由相信處決這些掃羅的後裔是贖罪的人祭，因而必須在基遍執行，以為那個地點比較合適。
6.en:
**Hang them up.** The Gibeonites may have had in mind the incident recorded in Num. 25:4, where the heads of the people guilty of the crime of Baal-peor were to be hung “up before the Lord,” that “the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel.” The present situation was different, however, for instead of the guilty themselves being punished, the children were substituted.
Gibeah. The LXX reads “Gibeon,” which some regard as correct (see RSV). However, there is good reason to retain the reading of the Hebrew text. Gibeah was the home of Saul. (1 Sam. 10:26; 11:4). It would seem fitting that expiation for Saul’s crime be made at his ancestral home. It is true that at that time there was a national shrine at Gibeon, the place where the tabernacle then stood and where the Israelites offered sacrifices (1 Kings 3:4; 1 Chron. 16:39, 40; 2 Chron. 1:3). But there is no reason to believe that the execution of these descendants of Saul was regarded as a propitiatory human sacrifice and that it therefore had to be carried out at Gibeon, as if it would be more acceptable there.

7.zh:
王因為曾與掃羅的兒子約拿單指著耶和華起誓結盟，就愛惜掃羅的孫子、約拿單的兒子米非波設，不交出來，

**指著耶和華起誓。**見撒上18:3；20:12-17。大衛向約拿單所發的莊嚴誓約要求他從基遍人復仇的提議中排除約拿單的兒子。違犯了以色列的領袖們與基遍人所立的莊嚴誓約（書9:15,19-21），給以色列帶來了這一場大災難，所以大衛特別謹慎，免得違犯他曾與約拿單所立的莊嚴誓約。
7.en: **Because of the Lord’s oath.** See 1 Sam. 18:3; 20:12–17. The solemn oath that David had sworn to Jonathan required that he exempt the son of Jonathan from the proposed vengeance of Gibeon. The fact that the violation of the solemn oath of the leaders of Israel to the men of Gibeon (Joshua 9:15, 19–21), had brought this great calamity upon Israel, would cause David to be particularly careful that there would be no violation of the oath he had made to Jonathan.

8.zh:
卻把愛雅的女兒利斯巴給掃羅所生的兩個兒子亞摩尼、米非波設，和掃羅女兒米甲的姊姊給米何拉人巴西萊兒子亞得列所生的五個兒子

**利斯巴的兩個兒子。**利斯巴是掃羅的一個妃嬪，押尼珥曾被控與她通姦（撒下3:7）。
**所生的。**Yalad。亞得列是米拉的丈夫，而不是米甲的丈夫（撒上18:19）。米拉最初許給大衛，後來卻嫁給了亞得列，大衛則娶了米甲（撒上18:20-27）。除非米甲後來嫁給帕提育有子女（撒上25:44），否則她至死都沒有孩子（撒下6:23）。
8.en:
**Two sons of Rizpah.** Rizpah was one of the concubines of Saul, with whom Abner had been charged with committing adultery (ch. 3:7).
Whom she brought up. Literally, “whom she bore.” There is no valid reason for is translating the Hebrew verb, yalad, employed in this phrase, “to bring up.” The difficulty, of course, is that Adriel was the husband of Merab, not of Michal (1 Sam. 18:19). The simplest solution seems to be to accept the reading of two Hebrew manuscripts, one of the recesions of the LXX, and the Syriac, which here read “Merob” for “Michal.” Merab was the one who was originally to be given to David, but who was given to Adriel instead, David receiving Michal (1 Sam. 18:20–27). Unless Michal had children through her marriage to Phalti (1 Sam. 25:44), she died childless (2 Sam. 6:23).

9.zh:
交在基遍人的手裡。基遍人就把他們，在耶和華面前，懸掛在山上，這七人就一同死亡。被殺的時候正是收割的日子，就是動手割大麥的時候。

**動手割大麥的時候。**緊接在逾越節之後（利23:10,11,14），是在現在的四月中旬到月末。
9.en: **Beginning of barley harvest.** This was immediately after the Passover (Lev. 23:10, 11, 14), and would be the middle to the end of our April.

10.zh:
愛雅的女兒利斯巴用麻布在磐石上搭棚，從動手收割的時候直到天降雨在屍身上的時候，日間不容空中的雀鳥落在屍身上，夜間不讓田野的走獸前來糟踐。

**用麻布。**麻布可能是展開來作為帳篷，形成了一個簡易的避身處，供利斯巴守夜時用。
**直到天雨降在。**巴勒斯坦通常的旱季從春天一直持續到秋天。在正常情況下，這期間不會降雨（見本卷註釋第110頁）。那時發生這場不合時節的降雨，打破了乾旱，不知道是不是形成三年饑荒的原因。小麥的收割隨著大麥的收割（出9:31,32；得1:22；2:23），在那個季節雨極其罕見（撒上12:17,18；箴26:1）。記載這一事件表明利斯巴忠心守護的時間較長。
**不容空中的雀鳥。**被殺之人的屍體被暴露在風雨之中。這樣處死的人通常在他們被懸掛的當天就該埋掉（申21:22,23），但這次他們的屍體卻顯然暴露於風雨中。可能直到此時，落雨才會作為上帝重新祝福的證據。在東方，露天的屍體幾乎立即會被野獸或禿鷹吃掉（見撒上17:44,46；王上14:11；16:4；21:23,24；太24:28）。在這個漫長的嚴酷考驗中，利斯巴晝夜忠心地守護著她兒子們的屍體。
10.en:
**Took sackcloth.** The sackcloth was probably spread out as a tent to form a rough shelter for Rizpah during her long vigil.
Until water dropped. The usual dry season in Palestine lasted from spring until fall. Under normal conditions there would be no rain during this period (see p. 110). Whether at this time an unreasonable rainfall occurred, breaking the drought that had probably been responsible for the three-year famine, we are not told. The wheat harvest follows the barley harvest (Ex. 9:31, 32; Ruth 1:22; 2:23), and rain is exceedingly rare at that season (1 Sam. 12:17, 18; Prov. 26:1). The recording of this incident indicates that Rizpah’s devoted watch was of long duration.
Neither the birds. The bodies of the slain men were left exposed to the elements. Ordinarily bodies of men who were thus executed were to be buried the day they were hanged (Deut. 21:22, 23), but in this instance their bodies were apparently left exposed, perhaps till such a time as the fall of rain would give evidence of God’s restored blessing. In the East a body left in the open would almost immediately become the victim of wild beasts or flocks of vultures (see 1 Sam. 17:44, 46; 1 Kings 14:11; 16:4; 21:23, 24; Matt. 24:28). Through this long ordeal, day and night, Rizpah kept a devoted vigil over the bodies of her sons.

12.zh:
大衛就去，從基列雅比人那裡將掃羅和他兒子約拿單的骸骨搬了來（是因非利士人從前在基利波殺掃羅，將屍身懸掛在伯珊的街市上，基列雅比人把屍身偷了去。）

**掃羅的骸骨。**利斯巴溫柔的忠誠使大衛對掃羅後裔表示尊敬（見13節）。大衛希望表現出他對先王沒有任何敵意，就把掃羅和約拿單的骸骨從基列雅比取來，備極哀榮地葬在他們的祖墳裡。
**街市。**直譯是“寬闊的露天地”，“廣場”。據撒上31:10-12，非利士人把掃羅和他兒子們的屍身釘在“伯珊的城牆上”，顯然這部分城牆面對著公共廣場。基列雅比人就是從這裡奪回了屍身（撒上31:11-13）。
12.en:
**Bones of Saul.** It was the tender devotion of Rizpah that caused David to show this respect for the descendants of Saul (see v. 13). Wishing to show that he cherished no enmity against the former king, David brought the bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabesh-gilead and gave them an honorable burial in the ancient family sepulcher.
The street. Literally, “the broad open place,” “the plaza.” According to 1 Sam. 31:10–12 the Philistines fastened the bodies of Saul and his sons to the “wall of Bethshan,” evidently on the section of the wall facing the public square. It was from this place that they were recovered at night by the men of Jabesh-gilead (1 Sam. 31:11–13).

14.zh:
將掃羅和他兒子約拿單的骸骨葬在便雅憫的洗拉，在掃羅父親基士的墳墓裡；眾人行了王所吩咐的。此後神垂聽國民所求的。

**洗拉。**便雅憫的一個城鎮（書18:28）。地點尚未確認，但可能靠近掃羅的祖先的家基比亞（見本卷註釋第459頁）。
**上帝垂聽。**類似的詞語見撒下24:25；創25:21；賽19:22。我們不必因聖經說“上帝垂聽”，斷定大衛為掃羅的錯行所做的事是遵循了上帝的計劃。耶和華可以根據激發行為的誠實的心衡量人的行為，即使祂譴責那行為本身。
14.en:
**Zelah.** A town of Benjamin (Joshua 18:28). It has not yet been identified but was probably near Gibeah, the ancestral home of Saul (see p. 459).
God was intreated. 2 Sam. 24:25; Gen. 25:21; Isa. 19:22 for similar expressions. Because the text states that “God was intreated” we need not therefore conclude that David had followed God’s plan for atoning for Saul’s evil deed. The Lord might measure an act by the sincerity of heart that prompted it, even though He condemned the act itself.

15.zh:
非利士人與以色列人打仗；大衛帶領僕人下去，與非利士人接戰，大衛就疲乏了。

指大衛與非利士人的另一次戰爭。《撒母耳記》的作者在這裡記錄了許多獨立的事件，它們與大衛作王期間其它事件的準確關係不得而知。這件事顯然發生在大衛統治了一段時間之後，所以年事已高（17節）。代上20:4-8中與非利士人這些爭戰的相應記錄，除了第一個之外，都緊接在約押毀滅亞捫的拉巴之後，《撒母耳記下》的作者將攻取拉巴放在撒下12:26-31中。《撒母耳記下》所插敘的事件——暗嫩的罪（撒下13），押沙龍從基述回來（撒下14），押沙龍（撒下15-19）和示巴（撒下20章）的叛亂以及三年的饑荒（撒下21:1-14）——在《歷代志》中都沒有記錄。
15.en: **Yet war again.** This refers to another war that David had with the Philistines. The writer of Samuel is here giving a number of detached items of which the exact relationship to other events in David’s reign is not known. The incident evidently took place after David had been ruling for some time and was therefore quite advanced in years (v. 17). In 1 Chron. 20:4–8 the parallel account of these struggles with the Philistines, except the first, follows the account of Joab’s destruction of Rabbah of Ammon, which the writer of 2 Samuel places in ch. 12:26–31. The intervening items of 2 Samuel—namely, Ammon’s sin (ch. 13), the return of Absalom from Geshur (ch. 14), the revolts of Absalom (chs. 15–19) and Sheba (ch. 20) and the three-year famine (ch. 21:1–14)—are not found in Chronicles.

16.zh:
偉人的一個兒子以實比諾要殺大衛；他的銅槍重三百舍客勒，又佩著新刀。

**三百舍客勒。**約7磅（3.4公斤）。歌利亞的槍頭重600舍客勒（撒上17:7）。
16.en: **Three hundred shekels.** About 7 lb. (3.4 kg.). The weight of the head of Goliath’s spear was 600 shekels (1 Sam. 17:7).

17.zh:
但洗魯雅的兒子亞比篩幫助大衛，攻打非利士人，將他殺死。當日，跟隨大衛的人向大衛起誓說：以後你不可再與我們一同出戰，恐怕熄滅以色列的燈。

**恐怕熄滅以色列的燈。**見王上11:36；15:14；詩132:17。大衛親自與敵人格鬥，常常使自己的生命處於危險之中。然而到了一個時候，王照著他的習慣與軍兵一同作戰不再明智也不必要了。
17.en: **Quench not the light.** See 1 Kings 11:36; 15:14; Ps. 132:17. David had frequently endangered his life by engaging in personal combat with his enemies. There came a time, however, when it was no longer wise or necessary for the king to venture into battle with his soldiers, as had been his custom.

18.zh:
後來，以色列人在歌伯與非利士人打仗，戶沙人西比該殺了偉人的一個兒子撒弗。

**歌伯。**在代上20:4的相應經文說這個事件發生在基色（代上20:4）。歌伯的地點不詳，可能在基色附近，是一個堅固的堡壘，俯瞰著伊磯倫東北約11.2公里、靠近亞雅侖谷的非利士平原。《歷代志》的作者記述這件事時，歌伯村可能已不為人知已了，於是作者就給出了在地理上較為著名的城鎮基色，現在是Tell Jezer。
**西比該。**這個名字也出現在大衛勇士的名單裡（代上11:29），但是在撒下23:27中，這個名字是“米本乃”。他是大衛軍隊第八班的班長（代上27:11）。
**撒弗。**在代上20:4的相應經文中為“細派”（代上20:4）。還加上一句“非利士人被制服了”。
18.en:
**At Gob.** In the parallel text this incident is said to have taken place at Gezer (1 Chron. 20:4). The site of Gob is not known, but it probably was in the neighborhood of Gezer, a strongly fortified bastion overlooking the Philistine plain about 7 mi. (11.2 km.) northeast of Ekron, near the Valley of Aijalon. It is possible that by the time the account in Chronicles was written, the hamlet of Gob had already become almost unknown and that the writer gave the geographical setting in terms of the much better known town of Gezer, now Tell Jezer.
Sibbechai. This name also occurs in the list of David’s heroes (1 Chron. 11:29), but in 2 Sam. 23:27 the name appears as “Mebunnai.” He was the captain of the eighth division of David’s army (1 Chron. 27:11).
Saph. Spelled “Sippai” in the parallel text (1 Chron. 20:4). The statement is also added there that the Philistines were subdued.

19.zh:
又在歌伯與非利士人打仗，伯利恆人雅雷俄珥金的兒子伊勒哈難殺了迦特人歌利亞。這人的槍桿粗如織布的機軸。

**在歌伯。**代上20:5的相應經文中沒有這個地名（代上20:5）。
**雅雷俄珥金。**或睚珥（代上20:5）。在代上20:5的相應經文中還有“歌利亞的弟兄拉哈米”。
19.en:
**In Gob.** The name of this place is omitted in the parallel passage (1 Chron. 20:5).
Jaare-oregim. Or Jair (1 Chron. 20:5).
The brother of. These words do not appear in the Hebrew of this verse but are taken from the parallel passage (1 Chron. 20:5), where also the name of Goliath’s brother is given as Lahmi.

21.zh:
這人向以色列人罵陣，大衛的哥哥示米亞的兒子約拿單就殺了他。

**罵陣。**該詞還用在撒上17:26,36,45。
**約拿單。**因而他是大衛的侄子（見代上20:7；撒上16:9），約拿達的兄弟，約拿達“為人極其狡猾”，曾是暗嫩的朋友（撒下13:3）。
21.en:
**Defied.** The same word that is used in 1 Sam. 17:26, 36, 45.
Jonathan. He was thus a nephew of David (see 1 Chron. 20:7; 1 Sam. 16:9), and a brother of Jonadab, the “very subtil man” who was the friend of Amnon (2 Sam. 13:3).

22.zh:
這四個人是迦特偉人的兒子，都死在大衛和他僕人的手下。

**偉人的兒子。**如果“偉人”被視為集體名詞或者指的是某一宗族的話，那麼這四個人就不一定是兄弟了，而只是迦特偉人族的後裔。
**他僕人。**`ebed，或“奴隸”，來自詞根`abad，意為“作工”或“服務”。這裡指為大衛服役的人。
22.en:
**Born to the giant.** If the word “giant” is considered a collective noun or as designating a certain clan, these four were not necessarily brothers, but simply descendants of the race of the giants in Gath.
His servants. Heb. ‘ebed, the usual word for “slave” or “servant.” ‘Ebed is from the root ‘abad, meaning “to work” or “to serve.” As here used, the term refers to those who served David as soldiers.

1.zh:
當耶和華救大衛脫離一切仇敵和掃羅之手的日子，他向耶和華念這詩，

**一切仇敵。**大衛在上帝非同尋常地將他從仇敵手中救出來之後寫了這首詩。這似乎不會在大勝亞捫人及其盟軍之前（見撒下8,10）。它好像是大衛還能在百姓面前講說他的公義和他手中的清潔時寫的（撒下22:21）。這必是在他對拔示巴和烏利亞犯罪之前（撒下11；參《先祖與先知》716頁）。
**脫離……掃羅的手。**這句話好像證明本詩不屬於大衛作王后期的作品，即使看起來象接近大衛作王結時的記錄。大衛得救脫離掃羅的手，連同他戰勝掃羅家餘剩的人，足以作為大衛寫這首詩的原因之一。這一結論似乎要求這首詩寫在大衛作王結束之前相當長的一段時間。
**這詩。**這首詩還出現在《詩篇》第18篇裡，多處有微小變動。第一節作為那首詩的標題。某些涉及大衛生平事件的其它詩篇也帶有解釋那些詩篇歷史背景的標題（參出15:1；申31:30；士5:1）。
1.en:
**This song.** The song also appears, with numerous slight variations, as Ps. 18. The first verse occurs as the title of that psalm. Certain other psalms that deal with incidents in David’s life carry titles that explain the historical setting of those psalms (cf. Ex. 15:1; Deut. 31:30; Judges 5:1).
All his enemies. David wrote this psalm after God had granted him a remarkable deliverance out of the hand of his enemies. That would not seem to have been until after the great victory over the children of Ammon and their allies (see chs. 8, 10). It also appears that the composition came while David could still speak before the people of his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands (ch. 22:21), which must have been before his sin against Bath-sheba and Uriah (ch. 11; cf. PP 716).
Out of the hand of Saul. These words tend to substantiate that the psalm does not belong to the last days of David’s reign, even though it here appears toward the close of the record of that reign. David’s deliverance from the hand of Saul, with his victory over the remnants of his house, was sufficiently recent to have been set forth by David as one of the reasons for the writing of the psalm. That observation would seem to require that the psalm be written some considerable time before the close of David’s reign.

2.zh:
說：耶和華是我的巖石，我的山寨，我的救主，

**說。**這句話出現在《詩篇》第18篇標題的結束語中。但那首詩的開篇“耶和華我的力量啊，我愛你！”在本節沒有出現。大衛所表達對上帝深切而溫柔的愛形成了整首詩的導言。
**耶和華是我的岩石。**這是大衛典型用語。大衛在逃避掃羅時經常在群山的岩石中找到避難所和力量。上帝對他來說就像岩石的力量一樣，給他提供保護並救他脫離他的仇敵。這首詩的風格特別具有大衛的特徵，充滿了莊嚴、力量與活力，自始至終瀰漫著大衛的全部精神。他曾那麼接近地生活在永恆的山嶺中，久居住在岩石中，以致它們已經形成了他的生命與生活的內在部分。將這些自然界的象徵交織到從他心中湧出的詩歌之中成了他的第二本性。
2.en:
**And he said.** These words appear as the last words of the title in Ps. 18. In that psalm, however, the opening words are: “I will love thee, O Lord, my strength.” This sentence does not appear here. David’s expression of his deep and tender love for God forms a fitting introduction to the psalm as a whole.
The Lord is my rock. This expression is typical of David. As a fugitive from Saul, David had often found the rocks of the mountains a refuge and strength. God was to him as the strength of the rocks, providing him protection and deliverance from his enemies. The style of the psalm is particularly characteristic of David, full of grandeur, strength, and vigor. The whole spirit of David pervades the psalm, from beginning to end. He had lived so close to the eternal hills, the rocks had so long been his abode, they had come to form an intrinsic part of his life and existence. It became second nature for him to weave these figures from the natural world into the songs that poured from his heart.

3.zh:
我的神，我的磐石，我所投靠的。他是我的盾牌，是拯救我的角，是我的高臺，是我的避難所。我的救主啊，你是救我脫離強暴的。

**投靠。**直譯是“避難。”這是大衛在《詩篇》第7篇和第11篇中奏出的勇敢之音。大衛已經學會了相信並信靠上帝。他知道無論人做什麼，上帝都不會使他失望。上帝就像永恆的山嶺一樣可靠。人可以完全信賴祂。
**我的盾牌。**對一個未曾參戰的人來說，盾牌的比喻沒有什麼價值或意義。但對於大衛來說，盾牌卻意味著生命本身。他從最生動的親身經驗得知它在生命的某些生死關頭是極其重要的。就像他可靠的盾牌經常擋住仇敵要擊倒他的猛刺一樣，上帝也屢次從敵人手中拯救了他的性命。這個比喻是大衛的特徵。他的詩歌活躍著並湧現著戰爭生活的精神，因為他是一個習慣於作戰的戰士。
**拯救我的角。**見路1:69。角是力量與權柄的象徵。這個比喻指獸的角，既用於收兵也用於進攻（見撒上2:1,10；詩75:10；89:17；92:10；112:9）。上帝是拯救大衛的角，在於祂不僅給他提供了保護和防衛，還在他與仇敵的積極作戰中幫助和堅固了他。
**我的高臺。**一個山上的要塞。在荒郊野外，這種地方通常很高，難以接近，易守難攻。因它很高，所以能俯瞰四圍的區域。它提供危險接近的警報並且處於抵抗進攻的有利位置。
**我的避難所，我的救主。**這句話在詩18:2沒有。它解釋了前面關於上帝的話，說明祂多麼受大衛尊敬。在需要之時，大衛可以逃到祂那裡避難，指望祂作為救他脫離看得見與看不見之仇敵的救主。
3.en:
**Trust.** Literally, “seek refuge.” This is the note of courage struck by David in Ps. 7 and 11. David had learned to place his faith and confidence in God. He knew that whatever man might do, God would never fail him. God was as sure as the rocks of the eternal hills. Man could place his complete trust in Him.
My shield. To anyone not a man of war the figure of a shield would have little value or meaning. To David the shield had frequently meant life itself. He knew from the most vivid of personal experiences its supreme importance in some of the critical moments of life. As his faithful shield had often warded off the thrusts of his enemies that were intended to lay him low, so God had repeatedly saved him from the enemy of his soul. The figure is characteristic of David. His songs live and breathe the spirit of the warlike life that was his as a soldier accustomed to battle.
The horn of my salvation. See Luke 1:69. The horn was a symbol of strength and power. The figure refers to the horns of beasts, that serve both to repulse and to make attacks (see 1 Sam. 2:1, 10; Ps. 75:10; 89:17; 92:10; 112:9). God was the horn of David’s salvation in that He provided him not only with protection and defense but with help and strength in active battle against his enemies.
My high tower. A mountain stronghold. In the wilds of the hills such a place was lofty, inaccessible, and safe from attack. From its heights a view could be obtained of all the surrounding area. It provided warning of approaching danger and also was a point of vantage from which to repel attacks.
My refuge, my saviour. These words are not found in Ps. 18:2. They explain the preceding declarations about God, showing how He was regarded by David. In time of need, David could flee to Him for refuge, and could look to Him as a Saviour from foes seen and unseen.

4.zh:
我要求告當讚美的耶和華，這樣，我必從仇敵手中被救出來。

**當讚美的。**將讚美歸於當受讚美的主是許多詩篇的一個顯著特徵。
4.en: **Worthy to be praised.** The ascription of praise to the One worthy to receive it is a prominent feature in many of the psalms.

5.zh:
曾有死亡的波浪環繞我，匪類的急流使我驚懼，

**死亡的波浪。**“死亡的悲哀”（詩18:4）。大衛此時想到迫近的危險，象洪水一樣要吞沒他。
**匪類的急流。**直譯是“彼列的急流”——毀滅性邪惡的化身。“毀滅的洪流”（修訂標準本）不斷地衝擊大衛，似乎要切斷每一逃生之路。他認識到撒但在與他的生命與靈魂作戰，惡人被那惡者用作工具，一直列陣與他作對。
**使我驚懼。**連最偉大的英雄有時也會被恐懼困擾。
5.en:
**The waves of death.** “The sorrows of death” (Ps. 18:4). David is here thinking of the dangers pressing about him, ever ready to engulf him as with a flood.
Floods of ungodly men. Literally, “the floods of Belial”—a personification of destructive wickedness. The “torrents of perdition” (RSV) were constantly sweeping about David, seeming to cut off every means of escape. He realized that Satan was warring against both his life and his soul, and that evil men, used as tools of the evil one, were ever arrayed against him.
Made me afraid. Even the greatest heroes are at times haunted by fear.

6.zh:
陰間的繩索纏繞我，死亡的網羅臨到我。

**陰間。**she'ol，比喻死人的領域，決不代表折磨人的地方。大衛經常九死一生。困苦、危險、迫害與危難是他每日的經歷。這些都使他接近上帝。
6.en: **Hell.** Heb. she’ol, the figurative realm of the dead. The term has nothing to do with a place of torment. David often experienced the nearness of death. Hardship, peril, persecution, and distress were his daily experience. These drew him close to God.

7.zh:
我在急難中求告耶和華，向我的神呼求。他從殿中聽了我的聲音；我的呼求入了他的耳中。

**求告耶和華。**大衛不斷被危險包圍著，開始認識到很少人曾認識到的：他不斷需要上帝之手的保護。危險使他祈求並指望耶和華的幫助。他所過的危險生活幫助鞏固了他深刻的宗教經驗。他的焦慮把他趕向上帝並使他親自熟悉了耶和華持續的指導與照顧。
**祂從殿中。**上帝從祂天上的居所俯看危險中的人，並賜給他們所需要的恩典與力量。大衛認出天上的聖殿是上帝的居所：“耶和華在祂的聖殿裡，耶和華的寶座在天上”（詩11:4）。
7.en:
**Upon the Lord.** Constantly surrounded by perils, David came to realize, as few men have, his continual need of the protecting hand of God. Danger caused him to pray and to look to the Lord for help. The perilous life he lived helped to confirm his deep religious experience. His anxieties drew him to God and gave him a personal acquaintance with the Lord’s constant guidance and care.
Out of his temple. From God’s heavenly dwelling place He looks down upon men in their distress and sends them the needed grace and strength. David recognized the temple of heaven as the abiding place of God: “The Lord is in his holy temple, the Lord’s throne is in heaven” (Ps. 11:4).

8.zh:
那時因他發怒，地就搖撼戰抖；天的根基也震動搖撼。

**因祂發怒。**把地的恐怖搖撼和天的驚人動盪說成是上帝發怒的可怕結果。
**搖撼戰抖。**8-16節含有關於上帝的一個驚人美麗且感人至深的畫面。這段經文非常卓越地描繪了上帝的力量與權能的崇高莊嚴。這是一個可怕的暴風與地震的畫面，伴隨著濃煙與黑暗，閃電爆發雷聲隆隆，震耳欲聾，向大衛揭示了上帝的親自臨格。無疑這畫面來自大衛親身的經歷，當大衛在野外，處於大自然的風雨中，並且可能在為自己的性命與他的仇敵爭戰之時，顯示了上帝臨近給屬祂的人帶來了救恩。這景象使人回憶起在西奈山頒佈律法時所伴隨著的恐怖（出19:16-18）。
8.en:
**Shook and trembled.** Verses 8–16 contain a strikingly beautiful and impressive picture of God. The passage is unsurpassed in sublimity and solemnity in its description of the might and power of God. The picture is one of a terrible storm and earthquake, accompanied by dense smoke and darkness, the outbursts of lightning and deafening peals of thunder, revealing to David the personal presence of God. Undoubtedly the picture came as a result of personal experience, when to David, out in the open, exposed to the elements, and perhaps battling for his very life against his foes, was revealed the nearness of God in the salvation He brings to His own. The scene is reminiscent of the terrors accompanying the solemn giving of the law on Sinai (Ex. 19:16–18).
Because he was wroth. By a figure of speech the dreadful shaking of the earth and the terrible commotions in heaven are pictured as the result of the awful wrath of God.

9.zh:
從他鼻孔冒煙上騰；從他口中發火焚燒，連炭也著了。

**從祂鼻孔冒煙。**詩歌的形象語言描繪自然界壯觀各種力量來自上帝，要執行祂指定它們去做的毀滅之工。
9.en: **Smoke out of his nostrils.** In poetic imagery the spectacular forces of nature are pictured as proceeding from God to carry out their divinely appointed work of destruction.

10.zh:
他又使天下垂，親自降臨；有黑雲在他腳下。

**使天下垂。**就像在暴風雨中烏雲下沉，似乎要壓在樹木與山巒之上，這裡也描繪上帝在祂的憤怒中使天下垂。
10.en: **Bowed the heavens.** As in a storm the clouds descend, seeming to rest upon trees and hills, so God is pictured as bending the heavens in His wrath.

12.zh:
他以黑暗和聚集的水、天空的厚雲為他四圍的行宮。

**祂以黑暗……為祂四圍的行宮。**“祂以黑暗為藏身之處；以水的黑暗為他四圍的行宮”（詩18:11）。這是上帝以暴風雨兇險的黑暗作為祂居所的畫面。祂坐在那裡，看不見卻很近，對祂的仇敵施行報復（見申4:11；詩97:2）。
12.en: **Darkness pavilions round about him.** “He made darkness his secret place; his pavilion round about him were dark waters” (Ps. 18:11). The picture is of God taking up His abode in the threatening darkness of the storm. There He sits, unseen but near, executing vengeance upon His enemies (see Deut. 4:11; Ps. 97:2).

13.zh:
因他面前的光輝炭都著了。

**光輝。**在暴風雨的黑暗中出現了眩目的閃電。
13.en: **Through the brightness.** Against the darkness of the storm appear blinding flashes of lightning.

14.zh:
耶和華從天上打雷；至高者發出聲音。

**耶和華從天上打雷。**緊隨著閃電（13節）是雷暴聲，帶來了上帝對祂的仇敵的懲罰。詩18:13還加上“有冰雹火炭”。
14.en: **The Lord thundered.** Immediately after the lightning (v. 13) the crash of thunder is heard bringing down the judgments of God upon His enemies. Ps. 18:13 adds: “hail stones and coals of fire.”

15.zh:
他射出箭來，使仇敵四散，發出閃電，使他們擾亂。

**祂射出箭來。**詩77:17,18也描述隆隆的雷聲緊隨著閃電。詩歌的語言把上帝描繪為一個戰士，發出祂的箭，為了消滅祂的敵人（見申32:23；伯6:4；詩7:12,13；38:2；哀3:12,13）。
**使他們擾亂。**耶和華全然擊潰祂的仇敵，祂與他們的戰爭以他們的徹底毀滅告終（見出23:27；書10:10；士4:15,16；撒上7:10）。
15.en:
**He sent out arrows.** These flashes of lightning, followed by peals of thunder, are also pictured in Ps. 77:17, 18. God is portrayed in poetic imagery as a warrior sending forth His arrows for the destruction of His enemies (see Deut. 32:23; Job 6:4; Ps. 7:12, 13; 38:2; Lam. 3:12, 13).
Discomfited them. The Lord accomplishes the utter rout of His enemies, and His warfare against them results in their complete destruction (see Ex. 23:27; Joshua 10:10; Judges 4:15, 16; 1 Sam. 7:10).

16.zh:
耶和華的斥責一發，鼻孔的氣一出，海底就出現，大地的根基也顯露。

**鼻孔的氣。**見出15:8，摩西用詩歌描述以色列人出埃及，說耶和華用祂鼻孔的氣吹回紅海的水，使“海中的深水凝結”。
16.en: **The breath of his nostrils.** See Ex. 15:8, where in a poetical description of the Exodus, Moses pictures the Lord blowing back the waters of the Red Sea by a blast of His nostrils, causing the depths to be “congealed in the heart of the sea.”

17.zh:
他從高天伸手抓住我，把我從大水中拉上來。

**從大水中拉上來。**大衛描述了上帝在暴風雨中顯示憤怒之後，現在描寫上帝對他施行的拯救（17-20節）。大衛就像被從苦海中拯救出來一樣。
17.en: **Out of many waters.** Leaving his description of the wrath of God manifesting itself in the storm, David now describes the deliverance God had wrought for him (vs. 17–20). David was delivered as from a sea of troubles.

18.zh:
他救我脫離我的勁敵和那些恨我的人，因為他們比我強盛。

**我的勁敵。**大衛在這裡可能直接指亞捫人及其盟軍（撒下10）。
18.en: **My strong enemy.** David here possibly refers directly to the Ammonites and their powerful allies (ch. 10).

19.zh:
我遭遇災難的日子，他們來攻擊我；但耶和華是我的倚靠。

**他們來攻擊我。**或“他們來阻止我”。

20.zh:
他又領我到寬闊之處；他救拔我，因他喜悅我。

**到寬闊之地。**與他的仇敵進攻所引起的極窄境遇形成對比。通過上帝的幫助，仇敵的勢力被打破，大衛得到了拯救。
**喜悅我。**大衛在這裡說明了上帝為什麼賜給他勝利而不給他敵人勝利的原因。這不是任意偏袒；上帝能為祂的僕人作奇妙的工作，是因為大衛與上天的計劃合作（見21-28節）。
20.en:
**Into a large place.** In contrast with the exceedingly narrow straits occasioned by the attacks of his enemies. Through God’s help the power of the adversaries was broken and David was delivered.
Delighted in me. David here gives the reason why God granted victory to him and not to his enemies. This was not an arbitrary favoritism; but God was able to work marvelously for His servant because David was cooperating with the program of heaven (see vs. 21–28).

21.zh:
耶和華按著我的公義報答我，按著我手中的清潔賞賜我。

**按著我的公義。**古時上帝應許健康與繁榮作為順從的直接賞賜（申28:1-14）。
**我手中的清潔。**手是行動的工具。耶和華既查看人們的行為也查看他們的心（詩15:2-5；24:4,5）。大衛在寫這些詩句時，能公開說他的手是清潔的，但是在他對拔示巴和赫人烏利亞犯罪之後就不可能這樣說了。據此我們能得到暗示：這首詩寫在擊敗亞捫人及其盟軍之後（撒下10），大衛與拔示巴犯罪之前（撒下11；見撒下11:1的釋）。
21.en:
**According to my righteousness.** Anciently God promised the blessings of health and prosperity as an immediate reward for obedience (Deut. 28:1–14).
The cleanness of my hands. The hands are the instruments of action. The Lord looks upon the deeds of men as well as their hearts (Ps. 15:2–5; 24:4, 5). At the time when these words were written David could speak openly of the cleanness of his hands, but that was not possible after his sin against Bath-sheba and Uriah the Hittite. We may have here an indication that this psalm was written after the defeat of the Ammonites and their allies (2 Sam. 10) but before David’s sin with Bath-sheba (ch. 11; see on ch. 11:1).

25.zh:
所以耶和華按我的公義，按我在他眼前的清潔賞賜我。

**按。**見21節註釋。

26.zh:
慈愛的人，你以慈愛待他；完全的人，你以完全待他；

**以慈愛。**在上一節中大衛說明了上帝賞賜他的原因。現在他寫下了普遍的原則，就是上帝確實會將同樣的憐憫和恩惠給予所有願意顯明自己是仁慈憐憫並正直的人。上帝的賞賜是受人對祂的態度和對同胞的行為這種條件限制的。然而約伯的經歷卻說明這一普遍原則可能有例外。由於基督與撒但之間大斗爭的牽連，有時苦難會被允許臨到義人身上，盡顧他們是公義的。
26.en: **With the merciful.** In the previous verse David has been setting forth the reason for God’s rewards to him. Now he lays down a general principle, again showing that the Lord had displayed no particular favoritism to him, that indeed God will extend the same mercies and favors to all who will show themselves merciful and upright. God’s rewards are conditioned by man’s attitude toward Him and his conduct toward his fellow men. However, the experience of Job illustrates that there may be apparent exceptions to this general principle. Because of the involvements of the great controversy between Christ and Satan, affliction is at times permitted to come upon the righteous in spite of their righteousness.

27.zh:
清潔的人，你以清潔待他；乖僻的人，你以彎曲待他。

**你以彎曲待他。**對於乖僻的人，上帝顯得乖僻。惡人感到祂對他們是不仁慈不公平的，而實際上祂卻是公正的，因為祂允許他們自食其果，照著他們對別人的行為受到相同的待遇。然而上帝設法藉著這一切拯救他們（見24>利26:23,24,40-45）。
27.en: **Shew thyself unsavoury.** To the perverse, God appears perverse. The wicked feel that He is unkind and unjust in His dealings toward them, when actually He is just, for He allows them to reap as they themselves have sown and permits the same treatment to befall them as they have accorded to others. Yet through it all God seeks to save them (see 24>Lev. 26:23, 24, 40–45).

29.zh:
耶和華啊，你是我的燈；耶和華必照明我的黑暗。

**你是我的燈。**“你必點著我的燈”（詩18:28）。本節開始了這首詩的另一部分（撒下22:29-46），大衛講述了耶和華過去和將為他所行的事（見詩132:17；王上11:36；15:4）。
29.en: **For thou art my lamp.** “Thou wilt light my candle” (Ps. 18:28). This verse introduces another section of the psalm. (2 Sam. 22:29–46) in which David tells what the Lord has done and will do for him (see Ps. 132:17; 1 Kings 11:36; 15:4).

30.zh:
我藉著你衝入敵軍，藉著我的神跳過牆垣。

**敵軍。**gedud。一支軍隊或輕裝的一群人，以搶劫為目的被派到敵國，比如燒燬洗革拉的亞瑪力人（撒上30:8,15）。大衛依靠耶和華的幫助，屢次戰勝這種敵方的搶劫隊。摧毀這種部隊需要速度、勇敢和能力，而上帝已經把這種才幹賜給了大衛。
**跳過牆垣。**在上帝的幫助下，沒有什麼障礙能夠阻止大衛追擊敵人。
30.en:
**Troop.** Heb. gedud. A division of the army or a group of light-armed men sent against an enemy country for purposes of plunder, such as the Amalekites, who burned Ziklag (1 Sam. 30:8, 15). Against such hostile bands David had repeatedly been victorious through the help of the Lord. It required speed, courage, and power to crush such forces, and this ability had been given to David by God.
Leaped over a wall. With God’s help no barrier was able to stop David in his pursuit of the enemy.

31.zh:
至於神，他的道是完全的；耶和華的話是煉淨的。凡投靠他的，他便作他們的盾牌。

**完全的。**Tamim，“完整的，”“全部的。”
**盾牌。**參第3節。上帝向所有信靠祂的人提供保護。
31.en:
**Perfect.** Heb. tamim, “complete,” “whole” “entire.” The emphasis of the Hebrew is not, as is the English, upon flawlessness, but upon completeness.
A buckler. Or a “shield” as in v. 3. God offers protection to all who place their trust in Him.

32.zh:
除了耶和華，誰是神呢？除了我們的神，誰是磐石呢？

誰是上帝呢？只有一位上帝，那就是耶和華。因此祂容許祂的敵人去實行自己的詭計，而祂卻掌有天上所有的力量。
誰是磐石呢？除了我們的上帝，誰是值得信賴的，堅定的，不改變的，可靠的呢？
32.en:
**For who is God? There was only one God, and that was Jehovah.** That being so, His enemies were left to their own devices, whereas He had all the power of heaven at His command.
Who is a rock? Who is trustworthy, firm, immovable, and sure, save our God?

33.zh:
神是我堅固的保障；他引導完全人行他的路。

**上帝是我堅固的保障。**不依靠耶和華的人只能依賴自己的軟弱；但信靠耶和華的人卻有天上所有的力量與他同在。
33.en: **God is my strength.** The man who does not lean upon the Lord is no stronger than himself, but the man who trusts in the Lord has with him all the strength of heaven.

34.zh:
他使我的腳快如母鹿的蹄，又使我在高處安穩。

**如母鹿的蹄。**在崎嶇的峭壁和山間的迷蹤中，母鹿的蹄迅速而穩當。在指定給大衛的彎曲道路中，上帝使他行走穩當而安全。
34.en: **Like hinds’ feet.** Among the rough crags and the bewildering trails of the mountains the feet of the hind were swift and sure. In the tortuous paths that it was given to David to follow, God had caused him to walk sure-footedly and safely.

35.zh:
他教導我的手能以爭戰，甚至我的膀臂能開銅弓。

**教導我的手能以爭戰。**大衛是一個熟練而成功的戰士。他把這方面的成功歸於上帝。他並沒有從事自私或殘忍的戰爭，而是打耶和華的仗，因而他能指望上帝給他技能，也給他保護與指導。
**銅弓。**古時的戰士以他們開弓的力量自豪。耶和華賜給大衛力量和技巧能成功地使用武器。
35.en:
**Teacheth my hands to war.** David was a skillful and successful warrior, and in this he ascribes his success to God. He did not engage in selfish or ruthless warfare, but fought the battles of the Lord, and thus he could look to God for skill as well as protection and guidance.
A bow of steel. Literally, “a bow of bronze.” Ancient warriors were proud of their strength in bending the bow. The Lord had given David strength and skill to wield successfully the weapons of war.

36.zh:
你把你的救恩給我作盾牌；你的溫和使我為大。

**你的救恩給我作盾牌。**見弗6:17：“救恩的頭盔。”人在生命中遇到任何危險的最好保護就是上帝拯救的大能。
**溫和。**`anoth，直譯是“回應”，意義不明確。詩18:35是`anawah（溫和）。上帝仁慈溫和的謙虛（見詩113:6,7）向地上柔和謙卑的人顯明（賽57:15；66:2），使他們能升到最高的尊榮與成就。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《傳道論》第639頁；《今日的生活》第53頁；《給傳道人的證言》104頁；《證言》卷三第477頁。
36.en:
**The shield of thy salvation.** See Eph. 6:17: “helmet of salvation.” The best protection that any man can have for any of the dangers of life is the saying power of God.
Gentleness. Heb. ‘anoth, literally, “to respond.” The meaning is obscure. Ps. 18:35 has ‘anawah, literally, “humility,” which is obviously the correct reading. God’s kind and gentle condescension (see Ps. 113:6, 7) manifested to the meek and humble of earth (Isa. 57:15; 66:2) enables them to rise to the greatest heights of honor and achievement.

37.zh:
你使我腳下的地步寬闊；我的腳未曾滑跌。

**使我的地步寬闊。**在狹窄的地方，禰給我餘地使我能前進不受阻礙。“你行走，腳步必不至狹窄；你奔跑，也不至跌倒”（箴4:12；參詩31:8）。
**腳。**直譯是“踝。”上帝賜給詩人力量，以堅定平穩的步伐行走在危險之地；他的腳踝不顫抖，腳也不滑跌。
37.en:
**Enlarged my steps.** In strait and narrow places Thou hast given me free room so that I was able to advance without hindrance. “When thou goest, thy steps shall not be straitened; and when thou runnest, thou shalt not stumble” (Prov. 4:12; cf. Ps. 31:8).
Feet. Literally, “ankles.” God gave the psalmist power to walk in dangerous places with a firm and even step; his ankles did not waver nor his feet slip.

39.zh:
我滅絕了他們，打傷了他們，使他們不能起來；他們都倒在我的腳下。

**我的腳下。**古代畫家經常描繪勝利者站在死在他們腳下或他們的戰馬腳下的敵人身上。這裡的畫面不是征服或統治，而是推翻和越過仇敵。
39.en: **Under my feet.** Ancient artists frequently pictured victors standing over their enemies who lay dead beneath their feet or beneath the feet of their horses. The picture here is not one of conquest and dominion but of casting down an enemy and passing over him.

40.zh:
因為你曾以力量束我的腰，使我能爭戰；你也使那起來攻擊我的都服在我以下。

**那起來攻擊我的。**在大衛的生涯中，仇敵不斷起來反對他，但是耶和華使他們倒在王的力量之前。
40.en: **Them that rose up.** In David’s career enemies were constantly rising up against him, but the Lord caused them to fall before the king’s might.

41.zh:
你又使我的仇敵在我面前轉背逃跑，叫我能以剪除那恨我的人。

**在我面前轉背。**意思是敵人在他面前轉背，被迫倉皇逃竄。參“我要使你一切仇敵轉背（希伯來文是頸項”（出23:27）。
41.en: **Given me the necks.** Or “given me the back of the necks.” The expression means that the enemies had been put to flight before him, having turned their backs on him. Compare, “I will make all thine enemies turn their backs [Hebrew, “necks”] unto thee” (Ex. 23:27).

43.zh:
我搗碎他們，如同地上的灰塵，踐踏他們，四散在地，如同街上的泥土。

**如同灰塵。**大衛的仇敵被摧毀如地上的灰塵，他們的能力歸於無有。詩18:42是：“如同風前的灰塵，”加上仇敵四散如同灰塵在風前四散的觀念。
**如同街上的泥土。**表示完全勝利的另一種說法。大衛的仇敵不僅被粉碎成塵土，還被踹在他的腳下（見賽10:6；亞10:5；瑪4:3）。
43.en:
**As the dust.** David’s enemies were pulverized as dust, their power being changed into impotence. Ps. 18:42 has: “as the dust before the wind,” thus adding the thought of scattering the adversary as dust is scattered before the wind.
As the mire of the street. Another expression denoting completeness of victory. Not only were the enemies of David crushed to dust, they were trodden underneath his feet (see Isa. 10:6; Zech. 10:5; Mal. 4:3).

44.zh:
你救我脫離我百姓的爭競，保護我作列國的元首；我素不認識的民必事奉我。

**我百姓的爭競。**詩18:43是“百姓的爭鬥，”如七十士譯本對撒下22:44的譯法。由於大衛被帶到對他的外國仇敵的徹底勝利的頂峰（撒下22:44-46），有人認為他幾乎不可能在這裡指國內的困難。他在這裡所從事他百姓的爭戰，是他們與別國開戰。
**列國的元首。**大衛征服外邦之後，成了他們的主人並接受他們的進貢。上帝的旨意並不是讓世界繼續分裂為許多國家，彼此不斷地爭戰。他們最終應該在一位王的領導之下合為一個國家，以耶路撒冷為首都。但以色列人拒絕配合上帝的計劃，不肯成為外邦人的領導者和擎光者。他們叛逆而驕傲，在許多方面與他們的外邦鄰居一樣壞。最後上帝棄絕了他們，並取消了他們的特權。
然而在將要作為大衛的子孫來臨的彌賽亞統治之下，通過上帝的真以色列——亞伯拉罕的屬靈子孫——那個計劃會在一定程度上實現，然而在許多方面卻與原計劃不同（見羅9:6-8；《先知與君王》703頁）。
**我素不認識。**見賽55:5。
44.en:
**The strivings of my people.** Ps. 18:43 has, “strivings of the people,” as does also the LXX of 2 Sam. 22:44. Since David is leading up to a climax of complete victory over his foreign foes (2 Sam. 22:44–46), some have thought it hardly likely that he would here be dealing with domestic difficulties. The wars of his people in which he was here engaged were wars that they were carrying on against other nations.
Head of the heathen. In his victory over the heathen, David had become their master and was receiving tribute from them. It was not the plan of God that the world should continue to be divided into many states constantly engaged in war against one another, but that they should ultimately be united into one nation under one king, with Jerusalem as the capital. But the Israelites refused to cooperate in God’s plan to make them the leaders and light bearers to the Gentiles. They were rebellious and proud, and in many respects no better than their heathen neighbors. Finally God rejected them and took away their privilege.
Yet under the Messiah to come as the Seed of David and through the true Israel of God—the spiritual seed of Abraham—that plan will receive a degree of fulfillment, yet different in many respects from the original design (see Rom. 9:6–8; PK 713, 714).
Which I knew not. See Isa. 55:5.

45.zh:
外邦人要投降我，一聽見我的名聲就必順從我。

**要投降我。**直譯是“要來奉承。”

47.zh:
耶和華是活神，願我的磐石被人稱頌！願神─那拯救我的磐石被人尊崇！

**耶和華是活神。**大衛在這裡開始了他這首詩的結尾部分（47-51節）。根據耶和華賜給他的勝利，他將讚美與感謝歸給上帝。耶和華並沒有忘記他或離棄他——祂永遠存在，是活神（詩42:2；賽37:4,17；耶10:10；何1:10；提前6:17），“獨一不死”的主（提前6:16）。對於大衛來說，上帝不僅是一種理論或抽象的概念——他已學會認識祂為個人的朋友和救主。他現在因祂奇妙的拯救和照顧向祂表示充滿感激的讚美。
**拯救我的磐石。**見詩89:26。大衛再次想起了上帝對他意味著什麼；祂既是他的磐石又是他的拯救，上帝是他的力量和保護，並給他帶來救恩。
47.en:
**The Lord liveth.** David here comes to the concluding section of his song (vs. 47–51). On the ground of the victories that the Lord has given him he ascribes praise and thanksgiving to God. The Lord had not forgotten him or forsaken him—He was ever present, the living God (Ps. 42:2; Isa. 37:4, 17; Jer. 10:10; Hosea 1:10; 1 Tim. 6:17), the one “who only hath immortality” (1 Tim. 6:16). God was more than a theory or a mere abstraction to David—he had learned to know Him as a personal Friend and Saviour, and he now expresses his grateful praise to Him for His wonderful deliverance and care.
The rock of my salvation. See Ps. 89:26. David again recalls What God means to him; He is both his rock and his salvation, the God who is his strength and defense and who brings salvation to him.

48.zh:
這位神就是那為我伸冤、使眾民服在我以下的。

**為我伸冤。**上帝活著並且照顧著。祂沒有讓大衛成為他仇敵手中無助的犧牲品，而是為他伸冤（見詩94:1；路18:7）。
48.en: **Avengeth me.** God lives and cares. He did not leave David a helpless victim in the hands of his enemies, but executed justice for him (see Ps. 94:1; Luke 18:7).

49.zh:
你救我脫離仇敵，又把我舉起，高過那些起來攻擊我的；你救我脫離強暴的人。

**救我脫離。**大衛屢次被敵人包圍，似乎無助並落在他們權下。但是上帝必賜給他拯救，救他脫離他們並使他們臣服在他以下。
**強暴的人。**有些註釋者認為該詞特指掃羅，但是其意義可能更為廣泛。從這首詩的整體內容，特別是結尾部分看，大衛並不是特指掃羅，而是泛指他的仇敵。這些人當然是強暴的人。要是大落在他們權下，他們必定虐待他。耶和華仁慈地救大衛脫離了這些人。
49.en:
**Bringeth me forth.** Repeatedly David found himself surrounded by his enemies and seemingly helpless and within their power. But God would grant him deliverance, bringing him victoriously out of their midst and placing them under subjection to him.
The violent man. Some commentators think that this phrase applies specifically to Saul, but the application is probably general. The whole content of the song, particularly the closing section, makes it seem that David is not thinking here specifically of Saul but of his enemies in general. These men were certainly men of violence, and if they could have gotten David within their power, they would have dealt cruelly with him. From such men the Lord had graciously granted David deliverance.

50.zh:
耶和華啊，因此我要在外邦中稱謝你，歌頌你的名。

**因此。**該詞把大衛獻上的感謝與先前關於上帝恩待他的敘述連接起來。大衛具有深刻的宗教經驗，其秘訣在於他經常記住他從上帝得到的憐憫，並不住地為此感謝耶和華。
**在外邦中。**賜給大衛的顯著勝利在列國面前高舉了以色列上帝的能力。保羅用這節經文說明認識上帝的知識如何會通過福音的傳揚進入到外邦人之中（羅15:9）。上帝計劃以色列成為祂拯救的佳音。詩人經常說到如果以色列能完成她的崇高使命，就會臨到她的榮耀。他展望到全地都敬拜上帝並唱詩讚美祂（詩66:4），以及地上所有的君王都在祂面前跪拜、列國都必侍奉祂的時候（詩72:11）。詩人呼籲以色列“將祂所行的傳揚在眾民中”（詩9:11）， “在列邦中述說祂的榮耀”（詩96:3），並表達他本人要在百姓中讚美上帝並在列邦中向祂歌唱的願望（詩57:9）。另見詩105:1；賽12:4。
50.en:
**Therefore.** The “therefore” links David’s giving of thanks to the preceding narration of God’s mercies to him. The secret of David’s deep religious experience lay in the fact that he constantly kept in mind the mercies he had received from God and never ceased thanking the Lord for them.
Among the heathen. The signal victories given to David exalted the power of Israel’s God before the nations. Paul quotes this verse to illustrate how the knowledge of God would go to the Gentiles through the preaching of the gospel (Rom. 15:9). God planned that Israel should be His evangel of salvation. The psalmist frequently spoke of the glory that would come to Israel if she would accomplish her high destiny. He looked forward to the time when all the earth would worship God and sing praises to Him (Ps. 66:4), and when all the kings of the earth would fall down before Him and all nations would serve Him (Ps. 72:11). Hence the psalmist called upon Israel to “declare among the people his doings” (Ps. 9:11) and “his glory among the heathen” (Ps. 96:3), and expressed his own intention to praise God among the people and to sing unto Him among the nations (Ps. 57:9). See also Ps. 105:1; Isa. 12:4.

51.zh:
耶和華賜極大的救恩給他所立的王，施慈愛給他的受膏者，就是給大衛和他的後裔，直到永遠！

**極大的救恩。**參詩18:50。意思很清楚：耶和華將祂豐富的救恩賜給王，使他大敗仇敵。
**他的後裔。**似乎指拿單在撒下7:12-16中的預言。在大衛睡後，耶和華會設立他的子孫接續他並堅立他國度的寶座到永遠。大衛現在為這偉大的恩慈感謝耶和華。整首詩是一首讚美與感謝的偉大聖歌，一首優美的抒情詩。大衛衷心地表達了他對上帝的信心，充滿感激地接受耶和華關於祂會把這國永遠賜給他和他的後裔的保證。
51.en:
**Tower of salvation.** Ps. 18:50 reads: “Great deliverance giveth he to his king.” The meaning is clear: the Lord bestows the fullness of His salvation upon the king, granting to him ever greater triumphs over his enemies.
To his seed. There seems to be a reference to the prophecy of Nathan in ch. 7:12–16, that after David fell asleep the Lord would set up his seed after him and establish the throne of his kingdom forever. For this great mercy David is now thanking the Lord. The whole psalm is a grand anthem of praise and thanksgiving, a beautiful and heartfelt expression of David’s confidence in God and of his grateful acceptance of the Lord’s assurance that He would give the kingdom to him and to his seed forever.

1.zh:
耶和華又向以色列人發怒，就激動大衛，使他吩咐人去數點以色列人和猶大人。

**發怒。**這裡沒有說明上帝發怒的原因。上下文暗示可能是源自以色列人因最近國力巨增而日益驕傲自信。成為世界強國的野心和效仿四圍列國的願望滋長了，而以色列國蒙召的莊嚴使命感卻下降了。
**就激動。**就是耶和華這麼做了。代上21:1相應的記錄是“撒但起來攻擊以色列人，激動大衛數點他們”。這兩句話並不一定是矛盾的，可能只是描述了同一件事的兩個方面。在本節中我們看到了又一個例子，就是把上帝所沒有阻止的事說成是上帝所做的（見《先祖與先知》728，739頁）。實際上是撒但鼓動了以色列王的驕傲和野心，使他推進擴大軍隊規模的計劃，目的是要通過新的軍事征服拓展以色列的邊界（見《先祖與先知》747頁）。
**數點以色列人。**記錄沒有這件事發生在大衛生平的什麼時候。約押進行這項工作差不多十個月（8節），表說明它必是發生在沒有戰爭的時期。代上24:21的相應經文記錄這件事緊接在大衛為建殿作預備之後。在《撒母耳記》和《歷代志》中，這些準備工作都列在大衛作王晚期的事件記錄中。這一切導致的結論是這次軍事統計發生在大衛作王快結束的時候。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–25節）**。《先祖與先知》第747-749頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–13節）**。《先祖與先知》第747頁。
1.en:
**Was kindled.** The cause of the displeasure is here not given. The context suggests that the source may have been the increased pride and self-confidence of Israel that resulted from the newly attained national greatness. Ambition for worldly greatness and a desire to be like the nations round about had arisen, and with it had come a decreasing sense of the solemn destiny to which the nation had been called.
He moved. That is, the Lord did so. The parallel account says, “And Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David to number Israel” (1 Chron. 21:1). These statements are not necessarily contradictory but may simply represent two aspects of the same incident. In the verse under consideration we have another instance where God is said to do that which He does not prevent (see PP 728, 739). It was actually Satan who instigated the pride and ambition that led Israel’s king to promote procedures to increase the size of his army for the purpose of extending the boundaries of Israel by new military conquests (see PP 747).
Number Israel. There is nothing in the narrative to indicate precisely when in the life of David this incident took place. The fact that Joab was engaged in the work for almost ten months (v. 8) shows that it must have been at a time of freedom from war. In the parallel account (1 Chron. 24:21) the narrative is immediately followed by the record of David’s preparations for the building of the Temple. In both Samuel and Chronicles these preparations are among the last items to be recorded for David’s reign. All this leads to the conclusion that the military census took place toward the end of David’s reign.

2.zh:
大衛就吩咐跟隨他的元帥約押說：你去走遍以色列眾支派，從但直到別是巴，數點百姓，我好知道他們的數目。

**吩咐……約押。**這件工作指派給約押，因為他是軍隊的元帥，而且這次數點是為了軍事目的（見9節；《先祖與先知》747頁）。
**從但直到別示巴。**代上21:2的順序是顛倒的“從別是巴直到但”（見代下30:5）。在所有早期的書卷—《士師記》，《撒母耳記》和《列王記》——都是“從但直到別是巴”（士20:1；撒上3:20；撒下3:10；17:11；24:2,15；王下4:25）。這種顛倒的原因可能是公元前約5世紀寫作《歷代志》時，在希伯來人的心目中早期王國最主要的部分是猶大，因為北國以色列在兩個世紀前就已經亡國了。由於但在北國，所以將它放在別示巴之前似乎不大合適。因此“從但直到別示巴”表明《撒母耳記》的成書日期較早。
2.en:
**To Joab.** The work was assigned to Joab because he was in command of the army, and the census was for military purposes (see v. 9; PP 747).
From Dan even to Beer-sheba. The phrase is reversed in 1 Chron. 21:2, “From Beer-sheba even to Dan” (see 2 Chron. 30:5). In all the earlier books—in Judges, Samuel, and Kings—the reading is “from Dan even to Beer-sheba” (Judges 20:1; 1 Sam. 3:20; 2 Sam. 3:10; 17:11; 24:2, 15; 1 Kings 4:25). A possible explanation for the reversal is that at the time when Chronicles was written, about the 5th century .., the part of the early kingdom uppermost in the Hebrew mind was Judah, for the northern kingdom of Israel had ended two centuries earlier. Since Dan was in the northern kingdom, it would hardly have seemed appropriate to name it before Beersheba. Thus the use of this expression, “from Dan even to Beer-sheba,” is an indication of the early date of the books of Samuel.

3.zh:
約押對王說：無論百姓多少，願耶和華─你的神再加增百倍，使我主我王親眼得見。我主我王何必喜悅行這事呢？

何必？約押是一個冷酷而肆無忌憚的將領，但是就連他都能看出採取這種數點措施不符合希伯來王國的基本原則。他用許多問題努力使大衛認識到他行這事的愚昧。
3.en: Why? Joab was a hardened and unscrupulous general, but even he could see that the taking of such a census was out of keeping with the fundamental principles of the Hebrew monarchy. By a number of questions he endeavored to cause David to recognize the folly of his course.

5.zh:
他們過了約但河，在迦得谷中、城的右邊亞羅珥安營，與雅謝相對，

**他們過了約旦何。**數點的這些細節在《歷代志》中省略了。約押和眾軍長過了約旦河就從南端的亞羅珥開始工作。這座城位於亞嫩河岸（申2:36；書13:16），在外約旦以色列領土的南邊界上。其遺址的名字仍是`Arâ`ir。
**河中。**或“谷中”（見書13:9）。
**迦得。**七十士譯本的一個修訂版為“向著迦得”或“直到迦得”。
**雅謝。**在迦得邊境的一座城（書13:24,25）。
5.en:
**They passed over Jordan.** These details of the method of taking the census are omitted in Chronicles. Crossing the Jordan, Joab and the captains of the host began the work in the extreme south, at Aroer. This city was on the banks of the river Arnon (Deut. 2:36; Joshua 13:16), on the southern border of Israel’s territory in Transjordan. Its ruins still bear the name ‘Arâ‘ir.
Midst of the river. Or, “midst of the wadi” (see Joshua 13:9).
Of Gad. One of the recensions of the LXX reads “toward Gad” or “unto Gad.”
Jazer. A city on the border of Gad (Joshua 13:24, 25).

6.zh:
又到了基列和他停合示地，又到了但雅安，繞到西頓，

**基列。**基列位於加利利海東南，包括迦得和瑪拿西。
**他停合示。**關於這個地點和名稱我們毫無所知。七十士譯本的一個修訂版為“赫地的加低斯”。
**但雅安。**這是唯一一處“但”後面加上“雅安”的地方。“但”的意思毫無疑問，因為它曾兩次提到（2,15節）。這裡描述的是一個北端的地點，所以鄰近西頓比較合理（見書19:47；士18:27-29）。
**西頓。**雖然西頓在名義上屬於亞設支派，但它似乎從未被亞設人佔領過（士1:31,32）。
6.en:
**To Gilead.** Gilead lay to the southeast of the Sea of Galilee and included Gad and Manasseh.
Tahtim-hodshi. Nothing is known of this land and nothing whatsoever can be made of this name. One of the recensions of the LXX reads “Kadesh in the land of the Hittites.”
Dan-jaan. This is the only place where the name “Dan” appears with the suffix “jaan.” There is no question that “Dan” is meant, since it is twice referred to (vs. 2, 15) and since at this point in the description a place at the extreme northern limit, in the vicinity of Sidon, would be in order (see Joshua 19:47; Judges 18:27–29).
Zidon. Although Sidon was nominally within the tribe of Asher, it does not appear ever to have been possessed by the Asherites (Judges 1:31, 32).

7.zh:
來到推羅的保障，並希未人和迦南人的各城，又到猶大南方的別是巴。

**推羅的保障。**他們到了臨近推羅的腓尼基邊界的某個要塞，但沒有進入那座城本身。推羅當時是一個獨立的國家。它的王希蘭既是大衛的朋友（撒下5:11；代上14:1）又是所羅門的朋友（王上5:1）。
**希未人。**這些古代迦南居民的剩餘之人（申7:1；士3:5）似乎依舊佔據以色列邊境的某些部分。
**到別示巴。**沒有說明在以色列和猶大主要地區進行數點的任何細節。
7.en:
**The strong hold of Tyre.** They came to some strong place on the Phoenician boundary in the vicinity of Tyre, although they did not come to the city itself. Tyre was at this time an independent state whose ruler, Hiram, was a friend of both David (2 Sam. 5:11; 1 Chron. 14:1) and Solomon (1 Kings 5:1).
The Hivites. It appears that the remnants of these ancient inhabitants of the land (Deut. 7:1; Judges 3:5) still occupied portions on the borders of Israel.
To Beer-sheba. No details are given of the places visited in the taking of the census in the main parts of Israel and Judah.

8.zh:
他們走遍全地，過了九個月零二十天，就回到耶路撒冷。

**九個月零二十天。**這細節反映了記錄的可靠性。花了這麼長時間表明工作必須非常仔細。
8.en: **Nine months and twenty days.** This exact detail reflects the reliability of the record. The fact that so long a time was taken indicates the fact that careful work must have been done.

9.zh:
約押將百姓的總數奏告於王：以色列拿刀的勇士有八十萬；猶大有五十萬。

**總數奏告於王。**這裡的數字與代上21:5不同。有些人認為《歷代志上》的總數可能包括288,000人的現役部隊（代上27:1-15）。有人認為這個總數包括利未支派和便雅憫支派的估計人數，因為沒有數點他們（代上21:6）。本節的“勇士”和代上21:5的“以色列人”之間的區別，可能把前者看作符合現役條件的軍隊，把後者看作包括預備隊。無論如何，這些數字顯然都是大約數。
9.en: **Gave up the sum.** The figures given here differ from those in 1 Chron. 21:5. Some believe that the total assigned to Israel in Chronicles may have included the standing army of 288,000 men (1 Chron. 27:1–15). Others take this total to include estimates of the tribes of Levi and Benjamin, whose census was not taken (1 Chron. 21:6). Perhaps a distinction can be found between the “valiant men” here designated and the “all they of Israel” in 1 Chron. 21:5 by regarding the former group as troops eligible for active duty, and the latter as including, in addition, reserve units. In any case the figures as given are obviously round numbers.

10.zh:
大衛數點百姓以後，就心中自責，禱告耶和華說：我行這事大有罪了。耶和華啊，求你除掉僕人的罪孽，因我所行的甚是愚昧。

**我……大有罪了。**當數點還在進行的時候，大衛就開始仔細考慮他所做之事的含意，並認識到他正在犯錯誤。是上帝的靈對他說話並向他顯明他行為的愚昧。他深深謙卑中地在上帝面前承認了自己的罪並且請求赦免。
10.en: **I have sinned greatly.** As the census was under way, David began to think over the implications of what he had done and to realize that he was making a mistake. It was the Spirit of God that spoke to him and showed him the folly of his course. In deep humility he confessed his mistake before God and asked for forgiveness.

13.zh:
於是迦得來見大衛，對他說：你願意國中有七年的饑荒呢？是在你敵人面前逃跑，被追趕三個月呢？是在你國中有三日的瘟疫呢？現在你要揣摩思想，我好回覆那差我來的。

**七年。**七十士譯本為“三年”，與代上21:12的相應經文一樣。
13.en: **Seven years.** The LXX reads “three years,” as does the parallel passage, 1 Chron. 21:12.

14.zh:
大衛對迦得說：我甚為難！我願落在耶和華的手裡，因為他有豐盛的憐憫。我不願落在人的手裡。

**耶和華的手裡。**大衛此時似乎沒有作了一個絕對是他自己的判斷會做出的選擇，除非它是來自上帝的。瘟疫和饑荒都可以看作是直接來自耶和華的。兩種懲罰都該既臨到百姓和王，但是因為百姓懷有鼓動大衛進行數點的同樣的罪，所以耶和華藉著大衛的錯誤懲罰了以色列人的罪（見《先祖與先知》748頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給傳道人的證言》354頁；《證言》卷五第57頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–25節）**。《先祖與先知》第748頁。
14.en: **The hand of the Lord.** David does not here seem to have made an absolute choice as to exactly what his judgment should be, only that it should come from God. Either the pestilence or the famine might be regarded as coming directly from the Lord. Both judgments would fall upon the nation as much as upon the king, but inasmuch as the people cherished the same sins as those that prompted David’s action, the Lord through David’s error punished the sins of Israel (see PP 748).

15.zh:
於是，耶和華降瘟疫與以色列人，自早晨到所定的時候；從但直到別是巴，民間死了七萬人。

**到所定的時候。**指定了三天（13節）。
15.en: **To the time appointed.** The three days specified (v. 13).

16.zh:
天使向耶路撒冷伸手要滅城的時候，耶和華後悔，就不降這災了，吩咐滅民的天使說：夠了！住手吧！那時耶和華的使者在耶布斯人亞勞拿的禾場那裡。

**耶和華後悔。**見創6:6，出32:14註釋。
**亞勞拿。**或“阿珥楠”（代上21:15）。
16.en:
**The Lord repented.** See on Gen. 6:6, Ex. 32:14.
Araunah. Or “Ornan” (1 Chron. 21:15).

17.zh:
大衛看見滅民的天使，就禱告耶和華說：我犯了罪，行了惡；但這群羊做了什麼呢？願你的手攻擊我和我的父家。

**我犯了罪。**大衛坦率地承認自己的罪。他不想責備任何別人。他應該負主要的責任。他在上帝面前承認了這個責任。
17.en: **Lo, I have sinned.** David frankly confessed his sin. There was no attempt to cast the blame on anyone else. He was the one who was primarily responsible, and this responsibility he acknowledged before God.

18.zh:
當日，迦得來見大衛，對他說：你上去，在耶布斯人亞勞拿的禾場上為耶和華築一座壇。

**築一座壇。**天使停留的地點是在摩利亞。亞伯拉罕曾在這裡為獻以撒築了一座壇；上帝曾在這裡向他顯現的那座山（創22:1-14；代下3:1）。所羅門後來建聖殿也是在這裡。這個曾因憐憫止住死亡的地方是神聖的，此後被上帝的百姓公認為聖地（見《先祖與先知》748，749頁）。
18.en: **Rear an altar.** The spot where the angel halted was on Mt. Moriah, the mountain where Abraham had erected an altar for the offering of Isaac and where God had appeared unto him (Gen. 22:1–14; 2 Chron. 3:1), and it was here that Solomon later erected his temple. The place where death had been stayed by mercy was holy ground and was henceforth recognized as such by God’s people (see PP 748, 749).

23.zh:
王啊，這一切，我亞勞拿都奉給你；又對王說：願耶和華─你的神悅納你。

亞勞拿一知道大衛是為了建一座祭壇才要他禾場的，就樂意送給他，連同牛和打場的器具都送給他。為了使瘟疫止住，他樂於作出個人的犧牲。
23.en: **As a king.** This passage should read: “All these things, O king, does Araunah give unto the king.” As soon as Araunah knew that David desired the threshing floor for an altar he was willing to give it to him, together with the oxen and threshing instruments. He was willing to make his own personal sacrifice in order that the plague might be stayed.

24.zh:
王對亞勞拿說：不然。我必要按著價值向你買；我不肯用白得之物作燔祭獻給耶和華─我的神。大衛就用五十舍客勒銀子買了那禾場與牛。

**我必要……買。**大衛應該用錢購買這禾場而不是作為禮物接受，只有這樣才是正當的。大衛行事所根據的原則是所有真服務與犧牲的基礎。
**五十舍客勒銀子。**《歷代志》記錄的價錢是“六百舍客勒金子”（代上21:25）。可能《撒母耳記》的記錄中只涉及所購買的一個部分的價錢。大衛為“禾場與牛”付了50舍客勒銀子（570克，或1又1/4磅）。《歷代志》說他用600舍客勒金子（6.84千克，或15磅）買了“那地”。“那地”可能指整座摩利亞山，後來在其上建造了聖殿。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷二第127頁。
24.en:
**I will surely buy it.** It was only right that David should purchase the threshing floor for money and not accept it as a gift. The principle on which David acted underlies all true service and sacrifice.
Fifty shekels of silver. Chronicles gives the price as “six hundred shekels of gold” (1 Chron. 21:25). It may be that the record in Samuel deals with the price paid for only one part of the purchase. David paid 50 shekels (570 gm., or 1 1/4 lb.) of silver for the “threshingfloor and the oxen.” Chronicles states that he bought “the place” for 600 shekels (6.84 kg., or 15 lb.). “The place” may mean the entire hill of Moriah on which the Temple was later to be built.

25.zh:
大衛在那裡為耶和華築了一座壇，獻燔祭和平安祭。如此，耶和華垂聽國民所求的，瘟疫在以色列人中就止住了。

**獻燔祭。**當時的燔祭原是在基遍獻的，因摩西的帳幕在那裡（代上16:39,40；21:29；代下1:3-6）。代上21:26記錄當這些祭物獻上時，耶和華“就應允他，使火從天降在燔祭壇上”。大衛將這個地點定為耶和華殿的所在地（代上21:1；代下3:1）。
《撒母耳記下》最後記錄大衛的悔改並與上帝和好。大衛的一生，始終見證上帝的恩慈與憐憫，見證在那些真誠謙卑地獻身與祂之人經驗中祂救恩的大能。
25.en:
**Offered burnt offerings.** Burnt offerings at this time were offered at Gibeon where the Mosaic tabernacle then was located (1 Chron. 16:39, 40; 21:29; 2 Chron. 1:3–6). 1 Chron. 21:26 states that when these offerings were offered, the Lord “answered him from heaven by fire upon the altar of burnt offering.” David settled upon this site as the place for the house of the Lord (1 Chron. 21:1; 2 Chron. 3:1).
With this account of David’s repentance and reconciliation to God the book of Samuel closes. David’s life is a constant testimony to the goodness and mercy of God and to the power of His saving grace in the experiences of those who earnestly and humbly give their lives to Him.
